definition_zh: 反应；作出反应；起化学反应；反对
definition_en: to respond to something that happens; to undergo a chemical change; to act against something in opposition
core_image: 被按到底又猛地弹回的弹簧
scene: 手指一按，弹簧被压到底，松开后立刻弹了回来。 The crowd reacted with cheers when the goal was scored.
sceneCN: 这里 react 是「作出反应」（第 1 个义项：对某事作出回应）；句意为进球时人群报以欢呼。画面里可留意：被压下的弹簧、弹回的瞬间、欢呼的人群。

pos.zh: 反应；作出反应；起化学反应；反对

derivatives.zh: react 加 -or，指反应堆、反应器
react 加 -ive，指易起反应的、反应性的
re- 与 activate 复合，指使重新活跃

senses.title: To respond
senses.definition: to respond in speech, feeling or action to something that has happened
senses.definitionCN: 在言语、情感或行动上对发生之事作出回应
senses.example: The crowd reacted with cheers when the goal was scored.
senses.exampleCN: 进球时人群报以欢呼。
senses.why: Latin reagere meant to act back, and reacting is exactly acting back upon something that acted first.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 reagere 意为「回过来行动」，而 react 正是对先行动的事物回以行动。

senses.title: To undergo chemical change
senses.definition: of substances, to combine or change as a result of a chemical process
senses.definitionCN: 指物质因化学过程而结合或发生变化
senses.example: Sodium reacts violently with water.
senses.exampleCN: 钠与水剧烈反应。
senses.why: Chemistry borrowed the same idea of acting back: two substances act on each other and are changed by it.
senses.whyCN: 化学借用了同一个「相互作用」的想法：两种物质彼此作用并因此改变。

senses.title: To oppose
senses.definition: to act against something one disapproves of or resists
senses.definitionCN: 对自己不赞成或抵抗的事物采取对抗行动
senses.example: Many residents reacted against the new tax.
senses.exampleCN: 许多居民反对这项新税。
senses.why: When the action back is directed against a force or a rule, the word takes the sense of resisting or opposing.
senses.whyCN: 当回过来的行动指向某种力量或规则时，这个词便有了「抵抗、反对」的意思。

intro.en: React comes from Latin reagere, built from re-, back, and agere, to do or drive; the word literally means to act back.
intro.cn: react 来自拉丁语 reagere，由 re-（回）与 agere（做、驱动）构成；字面意思就是「回过来行动」。

items.en: Agere meant to do, drive or perform, and it is the source of act, action and agent.
items.cn: agere 意为做、驱动或执行，是 act、action、agent 的来源。

items.en: The prefix re- meant back or again, so reagere pictured a force returning upon its source.
items.cn: 前缀 re- 意为向后或再次，因此 reagere 描绘的是一股力量回向它的来源。

items.en: Reagere meant to act back or to respond to an action already under way.
items.cn: reagere 意为回过来行动，或对已经在进行的动作作出回应。

items.en: English took the word as react and applied it to people, to feelings and later to chemical substances.
items.cn: 英语把这个词借作 react，先用于人、情感，后来又用于化学物质。

items.en: Modern English uses react for responses of every kind, for chemical change, and for resistance to what is imposed.
items.cn: 现代英语用 react 指各种回应、化学变化，以及对强加之事的抵抗。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the derived forms; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of responding and resisting.
note.cn: 形近组收派生形式；近义组收表示回应与抵抗的动词。

entries.definition: A response or a chemical change.
entries.definitionCN: 回应或化学变化。

entries.definition: A device or plant where a reaction takes place.
entries.definitionCN: 发生反应的装置或设施。

entries.definition: Tending to react readily.
entries.definitionCN: 易于起反应的。

entries.definition: To make active again.
entries.definitionCN: 使重新活跃。

entries.definition: To answer or react to something.
entries.definitionCN: 对某事作出回答或反应。

entries.definition: To answer in words.
entries.definitionCN: 用言语回答。

entries.definition: To oppose or withstand.
entries.definitionCN: 反对或抵挡。

entries.definition: To act against something.
entries.definitionCN: 对某事采取对抗行动。

normalIntro.en: The word is literally act back: something acts first, and the response acts upon it in return.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词字面上就是「回过来行动」：某物先行动，回应再反过来作用于它。

normal.en: React is re- plus act, so it means to act back on what has just happened.
normal.cn: react 是 re- 加 act，意为对刚发生的事回以行动。

normal.en: People react to news, crowds react to a goal, and chemicals react with each other.
normal.cn: 人 react to 消息，人群 react to 进球，化学品彼此 react。

normal.en: React against is the phrase for resisting something you disapprove of.
normal.cn: react against 是表示抵制不赞成之事的短语。

normal.en: Reaction is the noun, reactor the thing where a reaction happens, and reactive the tendency to react.
normal.cn: reaction 是名词，reactor 是发生反应的装置，reactive 是易反应的倾向。

normal.en: A slow reaction and a quick reaction differ in time, not in the word's meaning.
normal.cn: 反应慢与反应快，差别在时间，而不在这个词的意思。

abstract.en: To react is to prove that something outside you has reached you.
abstract.cn: react 就是证明身外之物已经触及了你。

abstract.en: What we react against often tells us what we value.
abstract.cn: 我们反对的东西，常常说明我们看重什么。

abstract.en: Every action leaves the world waiting for a reaction.
abstract.cn: 每一个行动都让世界等着一个回应。

examples.en: The crowd reacted with cheers when the goal was scored.
examples.cn: 进球时人群报以欢呼。

examples.en: Sodium reacts violently with water.
examples.cn: 钠与水剧烈反应。

examples.en: Many residents reacted against the new tax.
examples.cn: 许多居民反对这项新税。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「瑞阿克特」——弹簧被按下又弹回，记住 react 是反应、作出反应。

root: 拉丁语 re-（回）+ agere（做、驱动）→ reagere（回过来行动）→ 英语 react；同族有 reaction、reactor、reactive。

sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「回过来行动」；义项分为人的回应、化学变化与反对。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a spring pressed down and snapping back as soon as the finger lifts.
core.cn: 核心意象：弹簧被压下，手指一松便立刻弹回。

branches.en: a crowd cheering a goal
branches.cn: 为进球欢呼的人群

branches.en: a human answer and a chemical answer
branches.cn: 人的回应与化学的回应

branches.en: responding to a change and resisting it
branches.cn: 对变化作出回应，也对其抵抗

intro.en: The word is a Latin borrowing, and its family is built from re-, agere and English suffixes.
intro.cn: 这个词借自拉丁语，其词族由 re-、agere 与英语后缀构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin agere, to do, and reagere, to act back, are the recorded sources.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 agere（做）与 reagere（回过来行动）是有记录可考的来源。

definition_zh: 遇到；遭遇；邂逅
definition_en: to meet someone or face something unexpectedly
core_image: 转过林间小路，突然与一只鹿面对面
scene: 我们在森林里遇到一只鹿。 We encountered a deer in the forest.
sceneCN: 这里 encounter 是「遇到」（第 1 个义项：意外遇见某人或某物）；句意：我们在森林里遇到一只鹿。

senses.title: To meet someone or something
senses.definition: to meet a person, animal, or thing, especially by chance
senses.definitionCN: 尤其指偶然遇见某人、动物或事物
senses.example: We encountered a deer in the forest.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在森林里遇到一只鹿。
senses.why: The word is built on a Latin phrase for coming face to face, so it stresses the meeting itself.
senses.whyCN: 这个词建立在拉丁语「面对面」的说法上，因此强调相遇本身。

senses.title: To face a difficulty
senses.definition: to experience or come up against a problem, danger, or opposition
senses.definitionCN: 经历或直面问题、危险或反对
senses.example: The team encountered several problems.
senses.exampleCN: 团队遇到了几个问题。
senses.why: A difficulty stands in one's path like a person, so meeting it becomes encountering it.
senses.whyCN: 困难像人一样挡在路上，因此与它相遇就变成遭遇它。

senses.title: A meeting or confrontation
senses.definition: an unexpected meeting or a short conflict between people
senses.definitionCN: 意外的会面或人与人之间短暂的交锋
senses.example: Their first encounter was brief.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的初次相遇很短暂。
senses.why: The verb becomes a noun naming the event of coming face to face.
senses.whyCN: 动词转化为名词，命名面对面相遇的事件。

intro.en: Encounter comes from Old French encontrer, from Latin phrases meaning in the face of.
intro.cn: encounter 来自古法语 encontrer，源于拉丁语中意为「面对」的说法。

items.en: In contrā means against or facing.
items.cn: in contrā 意为相对、面对。

items.en: Encontrer means to meet or come against.
items.cn: encontrer 意为相遇、迎上。

items.en: English borrows the verb as encounter.
items.cn: 英语借入这个动词，写作 encounter。

items.en: The noun appears for meetings and clashes.
items.cn: 名词义出现，指会面与冲突。

items.en: Encounter covers chance meetings and facing problems.
items.cn: 现代英语中，encounter 涵盖偶遇与面对问题。

note.en: Encounter is often unexpected; meet is neutral, and face stresses dealing with a problem.
note.cn: encounter 常指意外相遇，meet 中性，face 强调应对问题。

entries.definition: meets or faces something

entries.definition: met or faced something

entries.definition: meeting or facing something
entries.definitionCN: 正在遇到

entries.definition: to come together with someone
entries.definitionCN: 遇见；会面

normalIntro.en: Encounter means coming face to face, whether with a deer or a problem.
normalIntro.cn: encounter 意为面对面相遇，无论对象是一只鹿还是一个难题。

normal.en: We encountered a deer on the path.

abstract.cn: 想象两个人偶然相遇。

root: 古法语 encontrer，来自拉丁语 in contrā（面对、相对）。

sensesIntro.en: The word covers chance meetings, facing difficulties, and the event of a clash.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词涵盖偶遇、面对困难，以及交锋事件。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: coming face to face on a forest path.
core.cn: 核心意象：在林间小路上面对面。

branches.en: The base sense is meeting someone or something.
branches.cn: 基本义是遇见某人或某物。

branches.en: Difficulties can be met as if they were opponents.
branches.cn: 困难可以像对手一样被遭遇。

branches.en: The verb also names the event itself.
branches.cn: 动词也命名事件本身。

branches.en: Meeting and the meeting are one idea in two forms.
branches.cn: 相遇与相遇事件是同一概念的两个形式。

branches.en: A clash is a meeting that turns hostile.
branches.cn: 交锋是变成敌对的相遇。

intro.cn: encounter 含有拉丁成分 contra，意为相对、面对。

latinIntro.en: Contra, against, also appears in contrast and contradict.
latinIntro.cn: 意为相对的 contra 也出现在 contrast 与 contradict 中。

items.exampleCN: 前缀 en- 开启 encounter。

items.example: Contra is the heart of encounter.
items.exampleCN: contra 是 encounter 的核心。
encountering 标记正在进行的动作。

items.example: To encounter is to meet unexpectedly.

items.meaning: to look toward or deal with
items.example: To face a problem is to encounter it.
items.exampleCN: face a problem 就是遭遇它。

definition_zh: 青春；青年时期；年轻人；少年
definition_en: the period of life when one is young, or young people as a group
core_image: 操场上刚跑完一圈的脸，汗亮着，喘着还要再跑
scene: 校门口的公交车一停，背书包的人一下涌下来，站台立刻热闹起来。 He spent his youth working in his father's shop.
sceneCN: 这里 youth 是「青年时期」（第 2 个义项：年轻时的那段人生阶段）；句意为他年轻时在父亲的店里干活。操场上一张张刚跑完还喘着的脸，就是这个词的印象。

derivatives.zh: 由 youth 加 -ful 构成，义为「年轻的；有朝气的」
同一词根的形容词，义为「年轻的」
由 youthful 加 -ly 构成，义为「年轻地」

senses.title: The state of being young
senses.definition: the quality or state of being young, seen as a stage of strength and change
senses.definitionCN: 年轻这一性质或状态，被视为有力气、爱变化的阶段
senses.example: The first grey hairs made him think about his lost youth.
senses.exampleCN: 第一根白发让他想起了逝去的青春。
senses.why: The noun came from the adjective for young, so it names the condition rather than a person at first.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词来自表示年轻的形容词，所以它先指状态而不是某个人。

senses.title: The early period of life
senses.definition: the time of life between childhood and adult life, treated as a fixed period
senses.definitionCN: 童年与成年之间的那段时间，作为一个人生阶段
senses.example: He spent his youth working in his father's shop.
senses.exampleCN: 他年轻时在父亲的店里干活。
senses.why: Once the condition is bounded in time, it becomes a stage with a beginning and an end.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个状态被划出时间范围，它就变成了有始有终的一个阶段。

senses.title: The young people
senses.definition: young people taken together as one group in society
senses.definitionCN: 社会上作为一个整体的年轻人
senses.example: The club was built for the youth of the neighbourhood.
senses.exampleCN: 这个俱乐部是为附近的年轻人建的。
senses.why: A name for a quality easily slides onto the people who have it, so the stage becomes the crowd.
senses.whyCN: 表示性质的名词很容易滑到具有这种性质的人身上，于是阶段变成了人群。

senses.title: The individual lad
senses.definition: a young man, usually a teenager, in reports and police language
senses.definitionCN: 年轻男子，通常指十几岁的，多用于报道与警方说法
senses.example: Two youths were seen running from the gate.
senses.exampleCN: 有人看见两个少年从大门口跑出去。
senses.why: The group word slips back to a single member, which is why the plural youths names individuals.
senses.whyCN: 群体词又滑回单个成员，所以复数 youths 指的是一个个少年。

senses.title: The early stage of anything
senses.definition: the early period of an institution, art form, or movement
senses.definitionCN: 机构、艺术形式或运动的早期阶段
senses.example: The idea was formed in the youth of the internet.
senses.exampleCN: 这个想法形成于互联网的早期。
senses.why: Since the word marks early life, any growing thing can borrow it for its own early years.
senses.whyCN: 既然这个词指生命的早期，任何成长中的事物都能借它来说自己的早年。

intro.en: Youth comes from an Old English noun geoguþ, built on the same root as the adjective young.
intro.cn: youth 出自古英语名词 geoguþ，与形容词 young 同根。

items.en: The root supplied both an adjective for being young and a noun for the age of youth.
items.cn: 这个词根同时提供了表示年轻的形容词与表示青年期的名词。

items.en: geoguþ named the period of young age and also the young people of a place.
items.cn: 古英语 geoguþ 既指青年时期，也指一个地方的年轻人。

items.en: The form became youthe and then youth, with the th kept as a sign of the noun.
items.cn: 形式先为 youthe，后为 youth，保留 th 作为名词的标记。

items.en: The word spread to institutions and movements in their early stages.
items.cn: 这个词扩用到处于早期阶段的机构与运动上。

items.en: The plural youths settled for individual young men, especially in reports.
items.cn: 复数 youths 固定指一个个年轻男子，尤其见于报道。

note.en: Youth is compared with its own family and with words for the same stage of life.
note.cn: youth 与自己的词族以及表示同一人生阶段的词作对照。

entries.definition: having the qualities of youth
entries.definitionCN: 同根派生词，有朝气的，年轻的

entries.definition: not old
entries.definitionCN: 同根形容词，年轻的

entries.definition: young men, one by one
entries.definitionCN: 同根复数，一个个少年

entries.definition: the stage between childhood and adulthood
entries.definitionCN: 近义，青春期

entries.definition: the length of time one has lived
entries.definitionCN: 相关概念，年龄

entries.definition: the last stage of life
entries.definitionCN: 反义，老年

normalIntro.en: One root gives young, youth, and youthful, all pointing at the same stage of life.
normalIntro.cn: 一个词根给出 young、youth、youthful，都指向人生的同一阶段。

normal.en: Youthful adds -ful, meaning full of youth, and is used of looks and energy.
normal.cn: youthful 加 -ful，意为充满青春，用于外貌与精力。

normal.en: The noun keeps a th sound while the adjective keeps a ng sound, a common Old English pair.
normal.cn: 名词保留 th 音，形容词保留 ng 音，这是古英语常见的一对。

normal.en: The youth of a place can mean its young people, as in the youth of the neighbourhood.
normal.cn: the youth of a place 可以指当地的年轻人。

normal.en: Germans call young people die Jugend, a close cousin of the same root.
normal.cn: 德语称年轻人为 die Jugend，是同一词根的近亲。

normal.en: In news reports, a youth is one young man, which is why youths is plural.
normal.cn: 新闻里 a youth 指一个年轻男子，所以复数是 youths。

abstract.en: Picture a track after a race, faces red and shining, still wanting another lap.
abstract.cn: 想象跑完一圈的跑道，一张张脸红亮着，还想再跑一圈。

abstract.en: Picture a school gate that opens and pours out a wave of bags and voices.
abstract.cn: 想象校门一开，涌出一片书包和喊声。

abstract.en: Picture a museum wall of early drawings from a young art form.
abstract.cn: 想象一面展墙，挂着某门年轻艺术的早期作品。

examples.en: He spent his youth working in his father's shop.
examples.cn: 他年轻时在父亲的店里干活。

examples.en: The club was built for the youth of the neighbourhood.
examples.cn: 这个俱乐部是为附近的年轻人建的。

examples.en: Two youths were seen running from the gate.
examples.cn: 有人看见两个少年从大门口跑出去。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「犹思」——上了年纪的人夜里「犹思」当年跑操场的日子，那段还想再来一遍的岁月就是 youth。

root: 古英语 geoguþ，与形容词 geong（年轻）同根，属日耳曼语族，与德语 Jugend 同源。

sensesIntro.en: A name for the state of being young becomes a stage of life, then a whole generation, then one lad, and finally the early years of anything.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个表示年轻状态的名词，先变成人生阶段，再变成一代人、一个少年，最后成为任何事物的早年。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: fresh faces still ready to run again
core.cn: 核心意象：还想着再跑一圈的年轻面孔

branches.en: The condition of being young is where the noun began.
branches.cn: 年轻的状态是这个名词的起点。

branches.en: Bounded in time, the condition becomes a stage.
branches.cn: 划出时间范围后，状态成了一个阶段。

branches.en: The quality passes to the people who have it.
branches.cn: 性质转移到了拥有它的人身上。

branches.en: From the group the word narrows back to one young man.
branches.cn: 从群体又收窄到单个年轻男子。

branches.en: Anything growing can borrow the word for its early years.
branches.cn: 任何成长中的事物都能借它说自己的早年。

intro.en: Youth forms youthful with -ful, and the same root also gives the adjective young.
intro.cn: youth 加 -ful 构成 youthful，同一词根还给出形容词 young。

latinIntro.en: Latin used iuventus for youth, which appears in English in juvenile and rejuvenate.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语用 iuventus 表示青春，它出现在 juvenile 与 rejuvenate 等英语词里。

items.example: The youth of the town meet here.
items.exampleCN: 镇上的年轻人在这里聚会。

items.example: She still has a youthful voice.
A young bird left the nest.

definition_zh: 衬垫；护垫；便笺本；拍纸簿；填塞；轻步走
definition_en: a soft piece of material used for protection or comfort, a block of paper for writing, to stuff something with soft material, or to walk with soft quiet steps
core_image: 书桌一角压着一本被撕去几页的便笺本，纸页边缘参差不齐
scene: 书桌一角放着一本撕过几页的便笺本，旁边躺着一支笔。 She wrote the address on a pad by the telephone.
sceneCN: 这里的 pad 是「便笺本」（第 2 个义项：一叠可撕的纸）；句意为她把地址写在电话旁的便笺本上。图中可辨识物件：便笺本、撕开的纸边、笔。

derivatives.zh: 由 pad 双写 d 加 -ing 构成，义为「填充物；赘语」
由 pad 双写 d 加 -ed 构成，义为「有衬垫的」
由 note 与 pad 复合而成，义为「便笺本」

senses.title: A soft piece used for protection or comfort
senses.definition: a piece of soft material placed under or against something to protect it, soften it or make it more comfortable
senses.definitionCN: 垫在某物下面或贴着某物的柔软材料，用来保护、缓冲或增加舒适
senses.example: The chair needs a new pad on the seat.
senses.exampleCN: 这把椅子的座面上需要一块新衬垫。
senses.why: Pad first named a soft bundle used as a bed or a cushion, so the word starts with something yielding placed under the body rather than with any shape.
senses.whyCN: pad 最初指当作床铺或坐垫的软捆，所以这个词的起点是垫在身体下面的一块软东西，而不是某个形状。

senses.title: A block of paper for writing
senses.definition: a number of sheets of paper glued together along one edge so that they can be torn off one by one
senses.definitionCN: 把若干张纸沿一边粘在一起，可以一张张撕下来使用
senses.example: She wrote the address on a pad by the telephone.
senses.exampleCN: 她把地址写在电话旁的便笺本上。
senses.why: A writing pad is a flat block of sheets, and that flat soft block looks exactly like the cushion the word already named, so one word covered both.
senses.whyCN: 便笺本是一叠压平的纸，而这个平整柔软的块状物，看起来正像这个词早先指的坐垫，于是一个词兼指两样东西。

senses.title: To stuff or line with soft material
senses.definition: to fill or cover something with soft material so that it is protected, fuller or more comfortable
senses.definitionCN: 用柔软材料把某物填满或包住，使它受到保护、更饱满或更舒适
senses.example: They padded the box with newspaper before posting it.
senses.exampleCN: 寄出之前，他们用报纸把箱子填塞好。
senses.why: The verb turns the cushion into an action: to pad something is to put a pad inside it, and from packing a box the sense spread to padding a speech with extra words.
senses.whyCN: 动词把坐垫变成动作：给某物加衬，就是往里面塞垫料；从给箱子填塞出发，这个意思又扩展到用多余的话把发言拉长。

senses.title: To walk quietly with soft steps
senses.definition: to walk with soft, quiet steps, especially with bare feet or paws
senses.definitionCN: 脚步轻软、几乎没有声响地走，尤指赤脚或动物用肉垫行走
senses.example: He padded across the room in bare feet.
senses.exampleCN: 他赤着脚轻轻走过房间。
senses.why: Bare feet or an animal's soft paw lands without a sound, and the word for a soft cushion became the verb for a walk that sounds like one.
senses.whyCN: 赤脚或动物的软掌落地几乎没有声响，于是「软垫」这个词又变成动词，指一种听上去像踩在垫子上的走法。

intro.en: The origin of pad is uncertain; the cushion sense is recorded in the sixteenth century, and one common suggestion links it to a Low German or Dutch word for the sole of the foot, but no origin is settled.
intro.cn: pad 的来源不确定；坐垫义在十六世纪已有记录，一种常见的推测把它联系到低地德语或荷兰语中表示脚掌的词，但没有定论。

items.en: The noun pad for a cushion appears in the sixteenth century, and dictionaries disagree about its source; a Low German or Dutch word for the sole of the foot is often suggested.
items.cn: 表示坐垫的名词 pad 在十六世纪出现，各词典对它的来源说法不一，常有人推测与低地德语或荷兰语中表示脚掌的词有关。

items.en: Pad named a soft bundle, a straw bed and a cushion, and it was also used for the stuffed saddle of a horse.
items.cn: pad 指软捆、草铺与坐垫，也曾用来指马背上加软垫的鞍。

items.en: The noun widened to any soft guard worn on the body, and the verb appeared with the sense of stuffing something with soft material.
items.cn: 词义扩展到身上穿的任何软护具，动词也随之出现，表示往某物里塞软材料。

items.en: A pad of paper named a block of sheets glued at one edge, and the verb gained the sense of walking with soft, quiet steps.
items.cn: a pad of paper 指沿一边粘住的一叠纸；动词也获得了脚步轻软地走这一义。

items.en: Modern English adds notepad, mouse pad and launch pad, keeps padding for stuffing material, and uses pad out for filling a text with needless matter.
items.cn: 现代英语加上 notepad、mouse pad 与 launch pad，保留 padding 表示填充物，也用 pad out 指用多余内容把文字拉长。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words built on pad or spelled close to it, including one false friend; the near-meaning group collects words for soft cushions, mats and paper blocks.
note.cn: 形近组收由 pad 构成或拼写相近的词，并收入一个假朋友；近义组收表示软垫、垫子与纸本的词。

entries.definition: Soft material used to fill or protect something, or needless words.
entries.definitionCN: 用来填充或保护的软材料，也指赘语。

entries.definition: Lined or filled with soft material.
entries.definitionCN: 加过衬垫或填过软材料的。

entries.definition: A small block of paper for taking notes.
entries.definitionCN: 用来记笔记的小本子。

entries.definition: A flat piece of material laid on a floor or a table.

entries.definition: A book of blank pages for writing notes.

entries.definition: A thick soft mass of material pressed together.
entries.definitionCN: 压在一起的一团软材料。

normalIntro.en: Pad is a short word for something soft and flat, and its hooks follow that flatness from a cushion to a block of paper and to a quiet footfall.
normalIntro.cn: pad 是一个表示「软而平的东西」的短词，记忆钩子顺着这份平整，从坐垫走到一叠纸，再走到一声轻软的脚步。

normal.en: Pad doubles its final consonant before a suffix, so the forms are padded and padding rather than paded.
normal.cn: pad 在加后缀前要双写末尾的辅音，所以形式是 padded 与 padding，而不是 paded。

normal.en: A pad of paper and a shoulder pad share one idea: a flat soft block that sits against something.
normal.cn: 一叠便笺纸与一块肩垫共有一个想法：一块平软的垫状物贴着别的东西。

normal.en: Padlock has nothing to do with a cushion, so the two words only look alike and must not be confused.
normal.cn: padlock 与坐垫毫无关系，两个词只是长得像，不能混为一谈。

normal.en: To pad a speech is to stuff it, exactly as a box is stuffed with paper before posting.
normal.cn: 给发言注水就是往里塞东西，和寄包裹前往箱子里塞纸一模一样。

normal.en: Pad across and pad along describe bare feet or soft paws, never the sound of heavy boots.
normal.cn: pad across 与 pad along 描写的都是赤脚或柔软的脚掌，绝不是沉重靴子的声响。

abstract.en: A word that means both a cushion and a notebook suggests that comfort and record-keeping can rest on the same flat softness.
abstract.cn: 一个词既指坐垫又指便笺本，说明舒适与记录可以建立在同一种平软之物上。

abstract.en: Padding protects a fragile thing and also makes it look bigger, which is why the same idea describes a parcel and a bloated essay.
abstract.cn: 填充既保护易碎之物，也让它显得更大，所以同一个概念既能说包裹，也能说一篇注水的文章。

abstract.en: Walking padded is walking as if the floor were a cushion, and the word quietly turns the ground into something kind.
abstract.cn: 轻步走就像把地板当成一块软垫，这个词悄悄把地面变成了温和的东西。

definition_zh: 回答；回应；反应
definition_en: an answer, or a reaction to something
core_image: 一个球被抛出去，又立刻被抛回来
scene: 她的回答简短而有力。 Her response was short and powerful.
sceneCN: 这里 response 是「回答」（第 1 个义项：对提问或信息的答复）；句意：她的回答简短而有力。

senses.title: A spoken or written answer
senses.definition: something said or written in reply to a question or message
senses.definitionCN: 针对问题或信息说出的、写下的内容
senses.example: I sent a short response to her letter.
senses.exampleCN: 我给她回了一封简短的信。
senses.why: The noun comes from Latin responsum, the thing promised or said back.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词来自拉丁语 responsum，即被回赠或回说之物。

senses.title: A physical or emotional reaction
senses.definition: a reaction of the body, mind, or system to something
senses.definitionCN: 身体、心理或系统对某事物的反应
senses.example: The medicine produced a strong response.
senses.exampleCN: 这种药产生了强烈的反应。
senses.why: A reply need not be verbal; any return effect is a response.
senses.whyCN: 回应不必是语言的；任何回馈效果都是 response。

senses.title: An organized reply to an emergency
senses.definition: the action taken by a group in answer to an emergency or appeal
senses.definitionCN: 群体针对紧急情况或呼吁采取的行动
senses.example: The flood response lasted three weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 这次洪灾应急响应持续了三周。
senses.why: An organized answer to danger is a large-scale extension of the reply idea.
senses.whyCN: 对危险的集体回应，是「答复」概念的大规模延伸。

intro.en: Response comes from Latin responsum, an answer, from respondere, to answer in return.
intro.cn: response 来自拉丁语 responsum（回答），源于 respondere（回以答复）。

items.en: Respondere means to answer in return.
items.cn: respondere 意为回以答复。

items.en: Responsum means an answer.
items.cn: responsum 意为回答。

normalIntro.en: Response is the ball thrown back: question goes out, answer comes home.
normalIntro.cn: response 是被抛回的球：问题出去，答案回来。

normal.en: In response to means as an answer to.

normal.en: A quick response is a fast answer.

normal.en: The body can have a strong response to medicine.

normal.en: Emergency response teams act during disasters.

abstract.en: Picture a ball bouncing straight back to the thrower.
abstract.cn: 想象球直接弹回投掷者手中。

abstract.en: Imagine a light switching on the moment a button is pressed.
abstract.cn: 想象按下按钮的瞬间灯亮起。

abstract.en: Think of a letter answered the same day it arrives.
abstract.cn: 想象一封信到达当天就得到回复。

examples.en: There was no response to our call.
examples.cn: 我们的呼叫没有得到任何回应。

examples.en: The audience gave the singer a warm response.
examples.cn: 观众给了歌手热烈的回应。

examples.en: The survey had a high response rate.
examples.cn: 这次调查的回应率很高。

root: 拉丁语 re-（回）＋ spondere（承诺）→ respondere（回以答复）→ responsum（回答）→ 英语 response，核心义「送回的回答或反应」。

sensesIntro.en: Response begins as a verbal answer, extends to any physical or emotional reaction, and finally to organized emergency action.
sensesIntro.cn: response 从口头回答开始，扩展到任何生理或情绪反应，最后指有组织的应急行动。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an answer returning to the source of the call.
core.cn: 核心意象：答复返回呼叫的源头。

branches.en: The verbal answer is the core sense.
branches.cn: 口头回答是核心义项。

branches.en: Any reaction extends the answer beyond language.
branches.cn: 任何反应都让回答超越语言。

branches.en: Organized emergency action is the public-scale sense.
branches.cn: 有组织的应急行动是公共规模义项。

branches.en: A patient and a reader both give back something.
branches.cn: 病人与读者都会给出回馈。

branches.en: Reacting to a flood becomes a coordinated response.
branches.cn: 对洪灾的反应发展成协调一致的响应。

intro.cn: response 是拉丁语「回答」名词，英语围绕同一词根构成 respond、respondent 与 responsive。

latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 spondere 意为承诺，responsum 意为回答。

definition_zh: 测量；测量结果；尺寸；度量单位体系；测定方法；评估；身体尺寸；测量误差；测量数据
definition_en: the act or process of measuring something, the figure or size obtained, or a system of units used for measuring
core_image: 木匠把卷尺拉过木板，把读数写进小本子
scene: 木匠把卷尺拉过木板，把量得的数字写进本子。 The carpenter pulls the tape across the board and writes the number in his notebook: that number is one measurement.
sceneCN: 这里 measurement 是「测得的尺寸」（第 2 个义项：测量结果）；句意：木匠把卷尺拉过木板，把那个数字写进本子，这个数字就是一次测量结果。图中可辨识物件：卷尺、木板、笔记本、铅笔、刻度数字；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 测量；测量结果；尺寸；度量体系；测定方法

forms.label: 单数（一次测量或测量这件事）
复数（多处尺寸或多组数据）

senses.title: The act of measuring: taking a reading
senses.definition: the act or process of finding the size, amount or extent of something with an instrument
senses.definitionCN: 用仪器求出某物大小、数量或延展的过程
senses.example: Careful measurement of the sample took an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 仔细测量这个样本花了一小时。
senses.why: The suffix -ment, from Latin -mentum, names the act or its product. This first sense keeps the act: the tape is stretched and a value is sought.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ment 出自拉丁语 -mentum，表示动作或其产物。第一个义项保留动作义：卷尺被拉开，人们要找一个数值。

senses.title: The result: a figure or size obtained
senses.titleCN: 测量结果：得到的数字或尺寸
senses.definition: the figure, size or amount obtained by measuring
senses.definitionCN: 测量得到的数字、尺寸或数量
senses.example: The measurements show a room of about thirty square metres.
senses.exampleCN: 测量结果显示这个房间约三十平方米。
senses.why: The same suffix also names what the act leaves behind. Once the tape is folded away, the number remains, and that number is also called a measurement.
senses.whyCN: 同一个后缀也指动作留下的东西。卷尺收起来之后，数字仍然在，这个数字同样叫 measurement。

senses.title: A system of units used for measuring
senses.titleCN: 度量体系：用于测量的单位系统
senses.definition: a system of units and standards by which quantities are expressed, such as the metric system
senses.definitionCN: 用于表示数量的单位与标准体系，如公制
senses.example: The laboratory converted all readings to the metric system of measurement.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室把所有读数都换算成公制计量体系。
senses.why: A number means nothing without a unit. The word therefore also names the shared scale itself, the system that makes readings comparable between labs and countries.
senses.whyCN: 没有单位，数字毫无意义。因此这个词也指共享的尺度本身，即让不同实验室、不同国家的读数可以互比的那套体系。

senses.title: The method or instrument used to measure
senses.titleCN: 测定方法：用何种手段量
senses.definition: the technique or instrument by which a quantity is determined, as in a measurement technique
senses.definitionCN: 确定某一数量的技术或仪器，如某种测量技术
senses.example: They changed the measurement method to reduce noise in the data.
senses.exampleCN: 他们改换了测量方法以减少数据中的噪声。
senses.why: The word moves from the act to the means of the act. Asking about 'the measurement used' is asking which procedure produced the number.
senses.whyCN: 词从动作转到动作的手段。问「用的是什么测量」，问的就是哪个流程产出了这个数字。

senses.title: Assessment: measuring performance or quality
senses.titleCN: 评估：把表现或质量当成量来测
senses.definition: the assessment of performance, quality or progress as if it were a quantity
senses.definitionCN: 把表现、质量或进展当作数量来评估
senses.example: Measurement of teacher performance is itself controversial.
senses.exampleCN: 对教师表现的评估本身就很有争议。
senses.why: What cannot be held with a tape can still be treated as a quantity. The word extends from physical size to judgement, and keeps the authority of the instrument.
senses.whyCN: 卷尺量不了的东西仍可被当作数量来处理。这个词从物理尺寸延伸到判断，同时保留了仪器的权威感。

senses.title: Body measurements: sizes taken for clothing
senses.titleCN: 身体尺寸：做衣服时量的三围
senses.definition: the set of body sizes taken with a tape, used for making or buying clothes
senses.definitionCN: 用软尺量出的一组身体尺寸，用于做衣或买衣
senses.example: The tailor took my measurements before cutting the cloth.
senses.exampleCN: 裁缝在裁布之前先量了我的尺寸。
senses.why: Here measurements is plural because a body yields several figures. The word keeps its plain physical sense but names a set rather than a single value.
senses.whyCN: 这里用复数，因为一具身体会得到好几个数字。词仍保留朴素的物理义，只是指一组值而非单个值。

senses.title: Precision measurement: readings and their error
senses.titleCN: 精密计量：读数与它的误差
senses.definition: the technical process of obtaining precise values, considered together with instrument error and uncertainty
senses.definitionCN: 获得精确数值的技术过程，并连同仪器误差与不确定度一起考虑
senses.example: Every measurement carries an uncertainty that must be reported.
senses.exampleCN: 每次测量都带有一个必须报告的不确定度。
senses.why: In metrology the word names a physical process with limits. Since no instrument is perfect, a measurement is always a value plus an admitted range of doubt.
senses.whyCN: 在计量学中，这个词指一个有极限的物理过程。仪器都不完美，所以测量永远是数值加上一个被承认的误差范围。

senses.title: Recorded readings: the data set
senses.titleCN: 测量数据：记录下来的一整套读数
senses.definition: the recorded set of readings taken during an experiment or survey
senses.definitionCN: 在一次实验或调查中记录下来的一整套读数
senses.example: The raw measurements were stored before any analysis.
senses.exampleCN: 原始测量数据在任何分析之前先被存了下来。
senses.why: Once readings are written down they become data. The plural then names a collection, and the word sits between the act of measuring and the analysis that follows.
senses.whyCN: 读数一旦写下就成了数据。复数于是指一个集合，而这个词正处在测量动作与随后分析之间的位置上。

intro.en: Measurement is the English noun measure plus -ment, from Latin -mentum, which names an act or its result. Measure came into English in the 14th century through Old French mesure from Latin mensura, the noun of metiri 'to measure'. The compound measurement is recorded in the 18th century, when scientific instruments made repeated readings a routine matter. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: measurement 是英语名词 measure 加 -ment，后者出自拉丁语 -mentum，表示动作或其结果。measure 在 14 世纪经古法语 mesure 进入英语，源自拉丁语 mensura，即 metiri「测量」的名词。measurement 这一复合形式在 18 世纪见于记载，当时科学仪器使反复读数成为常规。年代为大致估计。

items.en: Metric conventions and national standards bureaus make measurement a public, regulated activity rather than a craftsman's habit.
items.cn: 公制惯例与各国标准局的建立，使测量从工匠的习惯变成公共的、受规范的活动。

items.en: English measurement is recorded, formed from measure plus -ment as instruments and experiments spread.
items.cn: 英语 measurement 见于记载，随仪器与实验的普及由 measure 加 -ment 构成。

items.en: measure is borrowed through Old French mesure and covers a unit, a limit and the act of measuring.
items.cn: measure 经古法语 mesure 借入，兼指单位、限度与测量行为。

items.en: mensura is the noun of metiri; the same verb gives dimension, commensurate and immense.
items.cn: mensura 是 metiri 的名词形式；同一个动词还给出 dimension、commensurate、immense。

items.en: metiri rests on the reconstructed root *med- 'to measure, take the right size', which also gives modus and hence mode and moderate.
items.cn: metiri 建立在重构词根 *med-「测量、取恰当尺寸」上，该词根也给出 modus，进而有 mode 与 moderate。

note.en: The first group separates true relatives from a word that merely looks technical; the second compares words used in neighbouring parts of the same task.
note.cn: 第一组把真正的同族词与只是看起来专业的词分开；第二组比较同一件事相邻环节上的词。

entries.definition: the verb 'to find the size of' and the noun for a unit, limit or legislative step. Measurement is only the act or result, while measure also names the standard and the policy.
entries.definitionCN: 动词「测量」，名词指单位、限度或立法措施。measurement 只指动作或结果，而 measure 还指标准与政策措施。

entries.definition: the branch of geometry dealing with lengths, areas and volumes, or the act of measuring in a formal sense. It is the learned Latin-style counterpart, confined to technical writing.
entries.definitionCN: 研究长度、面积与体积的几何分支，或正式意义上的测量行为。它是学术性的拉丁式对应词，只用于技术写作。

entries.definition: a measurable extent such as length, width or height. It comes from dis- plus metiri, so it shares the measuring verb but names an extent rather than the act of measuring it.
entries.definitionCN: 可测量的延展，如长、宽、高。它由 dis- 加 metiri 构成，共享「测量」这个动词，但指延展本身，而不是测量的动作。

entries.definition: the act of judging the value or quality of something. It overlaps the figurative sense of measurement but does not require numbers.
entries.definitionCN: 对某物价值或质量的判断。它与 measurement 的引申义重叠，但不要求有数字。

entries.definition: the figure shown by an instrument at a moment. It is one measurement in the narrowest sense, taken off a dial or a display.
entries.definitionCN: 仪器在某一刻显示的数字。它是最狭义的一次测量，取自表盘或显示屏。

entries.definition: a defined indicator used to judge performance. It is a measurement chosen for a purpose, where measurement is the general obtaining of values.
entries.definitionCN: 用于评判表现的确定指标。它是为某个目的选定的测量，而 measurement 是一般的取值过程。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real pieces of the word and its real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想只使用这个词真实的构成成分和真实同族词，不用编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: -ment gives both faces of the word: the act of measuring and the figure that the act leaves behind.
normal.cn: -ment 给出这个词的两面：测量的动作，以及动作留下的数字。

normal.en: measure is the verb and the general noun; measurement is specifically the act or the result, never the policy.
normal.cn: measure 是动词兼一般名词；measurement 专指动作或结果，从不指政策措施。

normal.en: A measurement without a unit is just a number, which is why the word also names the system of units.
normal.cn: 没有单位的测量只是一个数字，所以这个词也指单位体系。

normal.en: The plural measurements usually means a set: body sizes, or a table of readings from an experiment.
normal.cn: 复数 measurements 通常指一个集合：身体尺寸，或实验读出的一整表数值。

normal.en: Measurement error is not a mistake but the admitted uncertainty that comes with every instrument.
normal.cn: measurement error（测量误差）不是错误，而是每件仪器都带来的、被承认的不确定度。

abstract.en: See a tape stretched, a number written, and a unit agreed: the three parts of every measurement.
abstract.cn: 想象卷尺拉开、数字写下、单位约定：这就是每次测量的三个部分。

abstract.en: The word travels from hand to page to report, and loses nothing but gains a claim to objectivity.
abstract.cn: 这个词从手上走到纸面再走到报告，什么也没丢，却获得了一种客观性的主张。

abstract.en: Whenever someone says 'by measurement', ask which instrument and which unit did the speaking.
abstract.cn: 每当有人说「按测量」，就该问：是哪件仪器、哪个单位在说话。

examples.en: Repeated measurement reduced the effect of random error.
examples.cn: 反复测量减小了随机误差的影响。

examples.en: The engineer sent the measurements to the factory.
examples.cn: 工程师把尺寸数据发给了工厂。

examples.en: Their claim rests on a single measurement taken at noon.
examples.cn: 他们的结论建立在正午所做的一次测量上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「没辙门特」——没辙时也得把门特（门）量一遍 → measurement 测量、尺寸

root: 拉丁语 metiri「测量」→ mensura「尺度」→ 古法语 mesure → 英语 measure；加 -ment（拉丁 -mentum，表示动作或结果）→ measurement。核心是「量这一动作，以及量出来的那个数」。

sensesIntro.en: All eight senses keep one image: a tape pulled across something. What changes is which part of the event is named — the pulling, the number, the agreed unit, the method, the judgement, the body being fitted, the error, or the whole table of readings.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都保留同一个意象：一条卷尺拉过某物。变化的只是命名了这件事的哪一段——拉尺的动作、数字、约定的单位、方法、判断、被量身的身体、误差，还是整张读数表。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a carpenter's tape stretched across a board, the figure written down.
core.cn: 核心意象：木匠的卷尺拉过木板，数字被写下来。

branches.en: THE ACT: the tape is stretched and a value is sought, which is measuring as an activity.
branches.cn: 动作：卷尺拉开去找一个值，这就是作为活动的测量。

branches.en: THE PRODUCT: one figure, or the whole recorded table of figures left after the act.
branches.cn: 产物：单个数字，或动作结束后留下的整张记录表。

branches.en: THE SHARED SCALE: units and standards make one lab's number comparable with another's.
branches.cn: 共享尺度：单位与标准让一个实验室的数字可与另一个实验室的比较。

branches.en: THE INSTRUMENT AND ITS LIMIT: the method produces the value, and every method brings its own uncertainty.
branches.cn: 仪器及其极限：方法产出数值，而每种方法都带来自己的不确定度。

branches.en: THE BODY AND THE JUDGEMENT: sizes taken for a suit, and performance treated as if it could be measured.
branches.cn: 身体与判断：为做衣量出的尺寸，以及被当作可测量的表现。

intro.en: Measurement is measure plus -ment, from Latin -mentum. That suffix names an act (as in movement) or its result (as in document), and measurement uses both faces.
intro.cn: measurement 是 measure 加 -ment，出自拉丁语 -mentum。这个后缀表示动作（如 movement「移动」）或其结果（如 document「文件」），measurement 两面都用上了。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is metiri 'to measure' with its noun mensura. The suffix -mentum also appears in document, monument and argument.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词基是 metiri「测量」及其名词 mensura。后缀 -mentum 也见于 document「文件」、monument「纪念碑」、argument「论点」。

items.meaning: the act of measuring, or the figure obtained
items.example: The measurement was repeated three times.

items.meaning: to find the size of, or a unit, limit or step
items.meaningCN: 测量；亦指单位、限度或措施
items.example: They measured the depth of the well.
The gain was measurable within a month.
items.exampleCN: 一个月内就有了可测的增益。

items.example: The measurability of pain is limited.
items.exampleCN: 疼痛的可测性是有限的。

items.meaning: having no limits that can be measured
items.meaningCN: 无边无际的；无法计量的
items.exampleCN: 他们穿过一片无边无际的平原。

items.structure: the same noun used for the technical process
items.meaning: the regulated process of obtaining values with instruments
items.meaningCN: 用仪器取得数值的规范过程

items.meaning: the formal or geometric measuring of lengths, areas and volumes
items.meaningCN: 测量术；几何中的长度面积体积计算
items.example: Mensuration is taught with areas and volumes.
items.exampleCN: 测量术是随面积与体积一起教的。

items.meaning: a measured extent such as length
items.example: Length is one dimension of the box.
items.exampleCN: 长度是这个箱子的一个维度。

items.meaning: measured by the same standard, and so proportionate
items.example: The fine was commensurate with the damage.

latinEntries.meaning: forms nouns of action or result
latinEntries.meaningCN: 构成表示动作或结果的名词

definition_zh: 家庭；一家人；家用的
definition_en: all the people living together in one home
core_image: 一张餐桌旁坐着一家人，桌上摆着日常用品
scene: 这个家庭每月都仔细记录开支。 The household records its spending carefully every month.
sceneCN: 这里 household 是「家庭」（第 1 个义项）；句意：这个家庭每月都仔细记录开支。

senses.title: All the people in a home
senses.definition: the people who live together as one unit
senses.definitionCN: 作为一个单位共同生活的人
senses.example: The household records its spending carefully every month.
senses.exampleCN: 这个家庭每月都仔细记录开支。
senses.why: This is the core sense of a domestic unit.
senses.whyCN: 这是家庭单位的核心义项。

senses.title: Relating to the home
senses.definition: connected with running a home
senses.definitionCN: 与操持家庭有关的
senses.example: Household goods are sold on the second floor.
senses.exampleCN: 家居用品在二楼出售。
senses.why: As an adjective the word describes home use.
senses.whyCN: 作形容词时描述家庭用途。

intro.en: Household joins house with hold in the old sense of possession.
intro.cn: household 把 house 与古义为「持有」的 hold 结合起来。

items.en: Hus meant a house.
items.cn: hus 意为房屋。

items.en: Healdan meant to hold or keep.
items.cn: healdan 意为持有或看管。

items.en: Houshold meant the people of a house.
items.cn: houshold 指一屋之人。

items.en: Household named a domestic unit.
items.cn: household 指家庭单位。

items.en: Household became an adjective for home goods.
items.cn: household 成为描述家居用品的形容词。

note.en: Household is compared with look-alike words and with words for family groups.
note.cn: 把 household 与形近词以及表示家庭群体的词作比较。

entries.definition: a building for living
entries.definitionCN: 房屋

entries.definition: a person who holds something
entries.definitionCN: 持有者

entries.definition: the head of a home
entries.definitionCN: 户主

entries.definition: parents and children
entries.definitionCN: 家庭

entries.definition: the place where one lives
entries.definitionCN: 家

entries.definition: a person's home
entries.definitionCN: 住宅

normalIntro.en: Household names a home as one unit of people and daily life.
normalIntro.cn: household 把家作为一个由人和日常生活组成的单位来称呼。

normal.en: The household records its spending carefully every month.
normal.cn: 这个家庭每月都仔细记录开支。

normal.en: All members of the household share the chores.
normal.cn: 家里所有成员分担家务。

normal.en: Household goods are sold on the second floor.
normal.cn: 家居用品在二楼出售。

normal.en: The brand became a household name.
normal.cn: 这个品牌变得家喻户晓。

normal.en: Household income rose slightly last year.
normal.cn: 去年家庭收入略有上升。

abstract.en: A household is a small economy built on shared daily needs.
abstract.cn: 家庭是建立在共同日常需求上的小型经济体。

abstract.en: To hold a house is to hold a set of relationships.
abstract.cn: 持有一个家，就是持有一组关系。

abstract.en: The word counts people the way a census counts homes.
abstract.cn: 这个词像人口普查统计住所那样统计人。

examples.en: The household records its spending carefully every month.
examples.cn: 这个家庭每月都仔细记录开支。

examples.en: All members of the household share the chores.
examples.cn: 家里所有成员分担家务。

examples.en: The brand became a household name.
examples.cn: 这个品牌变得家喻户晓。

dict_mnemonic.text: house 是房子，hold 古义为「持有、掌管家业」，household 就是「一屋之人、家庭」。

root: 由古英语 hus（房屋）与 healdan（持有）复合而成，原指一户人家及所掌管的家业。

sensesIntro.en: Household means the people of one home, or things used in the home.
sensesIntro.cn: household 指一屋之人，也指家庭使用的事物。

core.en: A home counted as one unit.
core.cn: 把家作为一个单位来计。

branches.en: The household records its spending carefully every month.
branches.cn: 这个家庭每月都仔细记录开支。

branches.en: All members of the household share the chores.
branches.cn: 家里所有成员分担家务。

branches.en: Household goods are sold on the second floor.
branches.cn: 家居用品在二楼出售。

branches.en: People and their goods both belong to the household.
branches.cn: 人与家用物品都属于这个家庭。

branches.en: The brand became a household name.
branches.cn: 这个品牌变得家喻户晓。

intro.en: Household forms householder and rests on house plus hold.
intro.cn: household 可构成 householder，词基是 house 与 hold。

latinIntro.en: Both halves are Germanic; the Latin equivalent appears in domestic.
latinIntro.cn: 两部分都属于日耳曼语；拉丁语对应说法见于 domestic。

items.meaning: all the people in a home

items.example: The holder of the ticket may enter.

latinEntries.example: Hus is the source of house.
