definition_zh: 损坏；损害；赔偿费
definition_en: harm done to something, or to harm it
core_image: 冰雹在车顶砸出一片细小的坑
scene: 冰雹过后，车顶多了一片密密麻麻的小坑。 The hail damaged every car on the street.
sceneCN: 这里 damaged 是 damage 的过去式，指「损坏」（第 2 个义项：使东西受损）；句意是冰雹砸坏了街上每一辆车。

senses.title: Harm done to a thing
senses.definition: physical harm that makes something less useful or sound
senses.definitionCN: 使某物变得不好用或不完整的实体损伤
senses.example: The storm caused damage to the roof.
senses.exampleCN: 暴风雨给屋顶造成了损坏。
senses.why: A thing is damaged when it can no longer do its job.
senses.whyCN: 当一个东西干不了它的活，它就是被损坏了。

senses.title: To harm something
senses.definition: to harm something or make it worse
senses.definitionCN: 伤害某物或使其状况变差
senses.example: The hail damaged every car on the street.
senses.exampleCN: 冰雹砸坏了街上每一辆车。
senses.why: Damage is what the blow leaves behind on the surface.
senses.whyCN: 损坏，就是那一击在表面上留下的东西。

senses.title: Money paid for harm
senses.definition: money paid to repair or make up for harm, usually in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 为修复或弥补损害而支付的钱，通常用复数
senses.example: The court ordered him to pay damages.
senses.exampleCN: 法院命令他支付赔偿金。
senses.why: When a thing cannot be mended, money is asked to stand in for it.
senses.whyCN: 东西修不好时，就请钱来代替它。

intro.en: Damage comes from Latin damnum, loss or cost, through Old French damage.
intro.cn: damage 源自拉丁语 damnum（损失、代价），经古法语 damage 进入英语。

items.en: Damnum meant loss, cost, or harm.
items.cn: damnum 意为损失、代价或伤害。

items.en: Damnare meant to cause a loss or condemn.
items.cn: damnare 意为使受损失或宣判。

items.en: Damage named harm and the loss it caused.
items.cn: damage 指伤害以及它带来的损失。

items.en: Damage entered English for injury to property.
items.cn: damage 进入英语，指对财物的损伤。

items.en: The plural damages named money paid in law.
items.cn: 复数 damages 指法律上支付的赔偿金。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the dam- opening, and the meaning group names other kinds of harm.
note.cn: 形近组共享 dam- 开头，近义组列出其他形式的伤害。

entries.definition: a wall that holds back water
entries.definitionCN: 挡水的墙

entries.definition: to condemn or swear at
entries.definitionCN: 谴责或咒骂

entries.definition: slightly wet
entries.definitionCN: 有点湿的

entries.definition: injury or damage to someone or something
entries.definitionCN: 对人或者物的损伤

entries.definition: harm done to a body
entries.definitionCN: 对身体造成的伤害

entries.definition: the fact of no longer having something
entries.definitionCN: 不再拥有某物的事实

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with hail on a car roof and end with a court order to pay.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从砸在车顶的冰雹开始，落到法院的赔付命令。

normal.en: Damage is the bill the world sends after a blow.
normal.cn: 损坏，是世界在打击之后寄来的账单。

normal.en: A thing is damaged when it stops doing what it was made for.
normal.cn: 东西做不了它原本该做的事，就是损坏了。

normal.en: Reputation can be damaged without a single broken object.
normal.cn: 名声可以被损害，却一件东西都没碎。

normal.en: When repair is impossible, damages are money in its place.
normal.cn: 修不好时，赔偿金就是代替它的钱。

normal.en: If it costs something to fix, there was damage.
normal.cn: 如果修它要花钱，那就是有过损坏。

abstract.en: Picture a car roof covered in small round dents.
abstract.cn: 想象车顶布满一个个小圆坑。

abstract.en: Picture a cracked window that still keeps out rain.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇裂了却还能挡雨的窗。

abstract.en: Picture a folded paper with a sum written at the bottom.
abstract.cn: 想象一张折起来的纸，末尾写着一个数额。

examples.en: The storm caused damage to the roof.
examples.cn: 暴风雨给屋顶造成了损坏。

examples.en: The hail damaged every car on the street.
examples.cn: 冰雹砸坏了街上每一辆车。

examples.en: The court ordered him to pay damages.
examples.cn: 法院命令他支付赔偿金。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 damage 记成「打折」：东西被打折了，就是受了损；修不好，就用钱来赔。

root: 源自拉丁语 damnum（损失、代价），经古法语 damage 进入英语；本义是让人遭受损失，先指财物的损伤，后指法律上为弥补损失而支付的赔偿金。

sensesIntro.en: From the harm a blow leaves, to the act of harming, to the money that stands in for what was lost.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一击留下的损伤，到使人受损的动作，再到代替损失的那笔钱。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hard blow landing on a surface and leaving a mark.
core.cn: 核心意象：一次重击落在表面上，留下痕迹。

branches.en: The noun names the harm itself.
branches.cn: 名词指伤害本身。

branches.en: The verb names the act that produces it.
branches.cn: 动词指造成它的那个动作。

branches.en: The plural turns the harm into a sum of money.
branches.cn: 复数把伤害变成一笔钱。

branches.en: The harm and the harming are two sides of one event.
branches.cn: 损伤与造成损伤，是同一件事的两面。

branches.en: What cannot be repaired is paid for instead.
branches.cn: 修不好的部分，就用钱来抵。

intro.en: Damage belongs to the Latin damnum family, where loss turns into harm and into money paid.
intro.cn: damage 属于拉丁语 damnum 这一族，「损失」在这里变成伤害与赔款。

latinIntro.en: The Latin damnum, loss, and damnare, to condemn, stand behind this family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 damnum（损失）与 damnare（宣判）是这一族词的根。

items.example: The damage was easy to see.

items.exampleCN: 破损的箱子被退了回来。

items.example: They damned the plan as foolish.
items.exampleCN: 他们谴责这个计划愚蠢。

items.example: The old tale warned of damnation.
items.exampleCN: 那个古老的故事警告人会有永罚。

items.example: He spoke damagingly of his rival.
items.exampleCN: 他说了有害于对手的话。
水灾损失导致道路封闭。

definition_zh: 含义；暗示；影响；牵连
definition_en: a meaning suggested but not stated, or a likely result that follows from something
core_image: 一句话说完后，听者脸上瞬间的迟疑
scene: 会上经理说预算「不会更少」，没人笑。 The implication was that someone would be let go, though nobody had said so.
sceneCN: 这里 implication 是「暗示、言外之意」（第 1 个义项：未明说而蕴含的意思），句意是言外之意是有人要走，尽管没人说出来。画面里有迟疑的听者和会议室。

pos.zh: 名词：含义、暗示、言外之意；影响、后果；牵连

senses.title: A meaning not stated
senses.definition: an idea that the speaker or writer suggests without saying it directly
senses.definitionCN: 说者或作者未明说却暗示的意思
senses.example: The implication of his remark was clear to everyone.
senses.exampleCN: 他那句话的言外之意人人都懂。
senses.why: The Latin root means folded in, and a hinted meaning is folded inside the words rather than laid out.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根意为「折进里面」，被暗示的意思正是折在话语之内，而未摊开。

senses.title: A likely result
senses.definition: a consequence that a decision or fact is likely to bring
senses.definitionCN: 某项决定或事实很可能带来的后果
senses.example: The finding has implications for food safety.
senses.exampleCN: 这一发现对食品安全有影响。
senses.why: A consequence is also folded inside a cause, waiting to unfold, so the same noun covers results.
senses.whyCN: 后果同样折在原因之内、等着被展开，于是同一个名词也涵盖结果。

senses.title: Involvement in wrongdoing
senses.definition: the fact of being involved in a crime or a scandal
senses.definitionCN: 卷入罪行或丑闻的事实
senses.example: His implication in the fraud ended his career.
senses.exampleCN: 他牵连进这起诈骗案，就此断送了事业。
senses.why: To be folded into an affair is exactly what involvement means, so the noun also reports guilt by association.
senses.whyCN: 被折进一桩事件，正是「牵连」，因此这个名词也用来报告「因关联而有嫌疑」。

intro.en: Implication is the Latin noun of folding in, and that physical image survives in every modern sense.
intro.cn: implication 是拉丁语的「折入」名词，这个具体意象在每种现代用法中都还活着。

items.en: Plicare meant to fold, and the fold could be cloth, a letter or an argument.
items.cn: 拉丁语 plicare 意为折叠，可折的是布、信，也可是一套论证。

items.en: Implicare folded something into something else, and hence entangled it.
items.cn: implicare 指把一物折进另一物，因而也指卷入、缠上。

items.en: Implicatio named that entanglement or the act of folding in.
items.cn: implicatio 命名这种缠绕，或折入的动作。

items.en: French used implication for involvement and for meaning carried within words.
items.cn: 法语用 implication 表示卷入，也指话语内含的意思。

items.en: Logic gave English the sense of what follows from a statement, now the commonest use.
items.cn: 逻辑学赋予英语「由陈述推出什么」这一义，如今是最常见的用法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the fold family; the near-meaning group gathers words for hinted meaning and consequence.
note.cn: 形近组收「折叠」词族；近义组收表示暗示与后果的词。

entries.definition: To suggest without stating, the verb behind this noun.
entries.definitionCN: 不说明而暗示，本名词背后的动词。

entries.definition: Folded in, not openly expressed.
entries.definitionCN: 折在其中的、不显明表达的。

entries.definition: A difficulty folded together with the main matter.
entries.definitionCN: 与主要事情绞在一起的麻烦。

entries.definition: A result that follows, closer to sense two.
entries.definitionCN: 随之而来的结果，接近第二个义项。

entries.definition: A hint or idea put forward softly.
entries.definitionCN: 轻轻提出的暗示或想法。

entries.definition: Being mixed up in an affair, close to sense three.
entries.definitionCN: 卷入某事件，接近第三个义项。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the folding image, which explains hidden meaning, hidden results and hidden guilt.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子用「折」这个意象，它同时解释了隐义、隐果与隐罪。

normal.en: Plic means fold, so implication is what is folded inside a sentence.
normal.cn: plic 意为折，implication 就是折进句子里的东西。

normal.en: Stress the third syllable: im-pli-CA-tion.
normal.cn: 重音在第三音节：im-pli-CA-tion。

normal.en: The verb is imply, the adjective implicit: all three wear the same fold.
normal.cn: 动词是 imply，形容词是 implicit，三者都带着同一个「折」。

normal.en: By implication is a useful phrase for reading between the lines.
normal.cn: by implication 是「读出弦外之音」的好用短语。

normal.en: Have implications for keeps the preposition for, not on.
normal.cn: have implications for 的介词是 for，不是 on。

abstract.en: A fold hides a surface and preserves it at once, which is why the word can mean both a secret meaning and a stored result.
abstract.cn: 折叠既藏起一面又保存它，所以这个词既能指隐藏的意思，也能指被存下的结果。

abstract.en: What is implied is present and absent at the same time, like an object under a cloth.
abstract.cn: 被暗示之物既在场又不在场，像布下的一件东西。

abstract.en: Arguments often move by implication, and the honest reader keeps unfolding the cloth.
abstract.cn: 论证常靠暗示推进，诚实的读者会不断把布展开。

examples.en: He objected to the implication that he had been careless.
examples.cn: 他反对那种暗示他不小心的说法。

examples.en: The new law has implications for every landlord.
examples.cn: 新法律对每个房东都有影响。

examples.en: She denied any implication in the scheme.
examples.cn: 她否认与这个计划有任何牵连。

dict_mnemonic.text: im 向内 + plic 折 + ation 名词——折进话里的意思：言外之意；折进事里的结果：影响

root: 拉丁语 plicare「折叠」→ implicare「折入、卷入」→ implicatio，经古法语 implication 进入英语，逻辑学使其定指「蕴含之义」。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: a hinted meaning, a likely consequence, and involvement in a case.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：暗示的意思、可能的后果，以及被卷进某桩事情。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pause on the listeners' faces after a sentence ends.
core.cn: 核心意象：话说完后，听者脸上那一瞬的停顿。

branches.en: THE MEETING LINE: the implication is that signals bad news.
branches.cn: 会议线：the implication is that 常引出坏消息。

branches.en: THE POLICY LINE: implications for whole industries.
branches.cn: 政策线：对整行业的影响。

branches.en: THE COURT LINE: implication in a fraud ends careers.
branches.cn: 法庭线：牵连进诈骗会断送前程。

branches.en: THE FOLD LINE: a hint and a result are both folded inside something.
branches.cn: 折叠线：暗示与结果都折在某物之内。

branches.en: THE CONSEQUENCE LINE: both senses report what follows from an act.
branches.cn: 后果线：两种用法都报告某种行为之后跟着来的东西。

intro.en: Implication is a Latin fold plus the noun ending -ation, in a family that includes imply and implicit.
intro.cn: implication 是拉丁语「折」加名词词尾 -ation，同族有 imply 与 implicit。

latinIntro.en: Plicare, implicare and implicatio are all recorded in Latin, so the folding image is documented.
latinIntro.cn: plicare、implicare 与 implicatio 在拉丁语中均有文献，「折」的意象有据。

items.example: The root also appears in complicate.

items.meaningCN: 表示动作或结果的名词词尾

items.example: Are you implying that I lied?
There is an implicit warning in the letter.

definition_zh: 缓解；减轻；接替；使摆脱；调剂
definition_en: to make pain, worry, or a difficult situation less serious
core_image: 拧得过紧的阀门被慢慢松开，压力随之下降
scene: 护士调慢了输液速度，药物在几分钟内让病人的疼痛明显减轻。 The nurse slowed the drip, and the drug began to relieve his pain within minutes.
sceneCN: 这里 relieve 是「缓解」（第 1 个义项：使疼痛或问题变轻）；句意：护士调慢了输液速度，药物在几分钟内开始缓解他的疼痛。

pos.zh: 缓解；减轻；接替；使摆脱；调剂

derivatives.zh: 由动词 relieve 去掉词尾构成，义为「宽慰；救济」
relieve 加 -ed 构成，义为「感到宽慰的」
加否定前缀 un- 与 -ed，义为「未获缓解的」

senses.title: To make pain or trouble less severe
senses.definition: to make a feeling of pain, worry, or pressure weaker or easier to bear
senses.definitionCN: 使疼痛、忧虑或压力的感觉变弱、变得容易承受
senses.example: This medicine will relieve your headache in about half an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 这种药大约半小时后能缓解你的头痛。
senses.why: The Latin source means to lift a weight, so easing pain is pictured as taking part of the load off.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词源意为「抬起重量」，因此缓解疼痛被想象成把部分负担从身上拿走。

senses.title: To take over a duty from someone
senses.definition: to take the place of someone who is on duty so that they can rest
senses.definitionCN: 替换正在值班的人，使其可以休息
senses.example: A fresh guard came to relieve the man at the gate.
senses.exampleCN: 一名新哨兵来替换门口的那个人。
senses.why: If a load can be lifted and handed on, then a duty can be lifted from one person and given to another.
senses.whyCN: 既然重物可以抬起并转交，那么职责也能从一个人身上卸下、交给另一个人。

senses.title: To free someone from something unpleasant
senses.definition: to take away a duty, worry, or possession from someone, often formally
senses.definitionCN: 把某项职责、忧虑或财物从某人身上拿走，常用于正式语境
senses.example: Let me relieve you of that heavy bag.
senses.exampleCN: 让我帮你拿那个重包吧。
senses.why: Lifting a weight off a person is the same motion as taking a burden or duty away from them.
senses.whyCN: 把人身上的重量抬走，与替他拿走负担或职务是同一个动作。

senses.title: To add variety to something dull
senses.definition: to make a boring or uniform situation more interesting by adding something different
senses.definitionCN: 通过加入变化，使枯燥或单调的场面变得有趣
senses.example: A few jokes relieved the tension in the room.
senses.exampleCN: 几个笑话缓解了房间里的紧张气氛。
senses.why: Relief is a lifting of pressure, and a dull stretch of time is felt as pressure that a change lifts away.
senses.whyCN: relief 的本质是卸下压力，而漫长的沉闷也像一种压力，变化正是把它抬走。

intro.en: Relieve comes from Old French relever, which descends from the Latin verb relevare.
intro.cn: relieve 来自古法语 relever，后者可追溯到拉丁动词 relevare。

items.en: Relevare combines re- with levare, to lift, and means to raise up or lighten.
items.cn: relevare 由 re- 与 levare「举起」组合，意为抬起或减轻。

items.en: Levare is built on levis, light in weight, which also gives levity.
items.cn: levare 建立在 levis「重量轻」之上，这个词根也产生了 levity。

items.en: Colloquial forms of relevare spread through the spoken language of the late empire.
items.cn: relevare 的口语形式在帝国晚期的日常语言中传播开来。

items.en: Old French relever means to raise again, to help up, and to ease.
items.cn: 古法语 relever 表示重新举起、扶起以及缓解。

items.en: English adopts relieve for easing pain, taking over a duty, and freeing someone of a burden.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪引入 relieve，用于缓解疼痛、接替职责以及替人卸下负担。

items.en: The modern verb keeps all three threads and adds the lighter sense of adding variety.
items.cn: 现代英语保留了这三条线索，并增添了「调剂、增加变化」这层较轻的含义。

note.en: Relieve is the verb behind relief and shares its lifting root with several light-related words.
note.cn: relieve 是名词 relief 背后的动词，并与若干表示「轻」的词共享抬起的词根。

entries.definition: the feeling that comes when pain or worry ends
entries.definitionCN: 宽慰；缓解，是 relieve 对应的名词

entries.definition: glad that a worry or pain has gone
entries.definitionCN: 感到宽慰的，由 relieve 加 -ed 构成

entries.definition: to make pain or suffering less severe
entries.definitionCN: 减轻；缓和，与 relieve 共享 levis 词根，只是前缀不同

entries.definition: to make pain or a problem less severe
entries.definitionCN: 减轻；缓和，语体比 relieve 更轻

entries.definition: to make someone calmer or make pain less sharp
entries.definitionCN: 安抚；使疼痛缓和，强调舒适感

entries.definition: to make a load or a mood less heavy
entries.definitionCN: 减轻；使轻松，保留了「重量」的比喻

normalIntro.en: Relieve is the verb form of the re- and lev- family, so its hooks all circle the idea of lifting.
normalIntro.cn: relieve 是 re- 与 lev- 词族的动词形式，所以记忆钩子都围绕「抬起」。

normal.en: Say the pair together: relief is the state, relieve is the act of bringing it about.
normal.cn: 把这一对一起记：relief 是状态，relieve 是带来这种状态的动作。

normal.en: The root lev- also lifts in elevate and lever, both about raising something.
normal.cn: 词根 lev- 在 elevate 和 lever 里同样表示「抬起」。

normal.en: Relieve someone of a bag means taking the weight into your own hand.
normal.cn: relieve someone of a bag 就是把重量接到自己手里。

normal.en: The past participle relieved doubles as the everyday adjective for feeling better.
normal.cn: 过去分词 relieved 同时也常用作形容词，表示「放心了」。

normal.en: Remember the fixed phrase relieve the pressure when talking about stress at work.
normal.cn: 谈到工作压力时，记住固定搭配 relieve the pressure。

abstract.en: Picture a valve turning loose and steam hissing out of a blocked pipe.
abstract.cn: 想象一个阀门被拧松，蒸汽从堵塞的管道里嘶嘶冒出。

abstract.en: Imagine handing a heavy suitcase to a friend at the top of the stairs.
abstract.cn: 想象在楼梯顶端把沉重的行李箱交给朋友。

abstract.en: See two guards saluting as one walks away and the other steps into place.
abstract.cn: 想象两名卫兵敬礼，一个走开，另一个站到岗位上。

examples.en: These tablets should relieve the swelling within a day.
examples.cn: 这些药片应该在一天之内缓解肿胀。

examples.en: I was relieved to hear that everyone was safe.
examples.cn: 听说大家都平安，我松了一口气。

examples.en: A new team will relieve the workers at midnight.
examples.cn: 一支新的队伍将在午夜替换这些工人。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞丽舞」——想象瑞丽的舞蹈让紧绷的人放松下来；只是谐音联想，并非词源。

root: 古法语 relever，源自拉丁语 relevare（re-「再次」+ levare「举起」，levis「轻」），核心为「把重量抬起」。

sensesIntro.en: All four senses are versions of the same act of lifting: lifting pain, lifting a duty, lifting a burden, lifting dullness.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项都是同一个「抬起」动作的不同版本：抬起疼痛、抬起职责、抬起负担、抬起沉闷。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tight valve loosened so that pressure falls.
core.cn: 核心意象：拧紧的阀门被松开，压力随之下降。

branches.en: Loosening pressure is felt first as less pain.
branches.cn: 松开压力最先被感受为疼痛变轻。

branches.en: Lifting a duty off one person puts it on another, which is the relieving shift.
branches.cn: 把职责从一人身上卸下交给另一人，就是接替。

branches.en: Taking a heavy thing out of someone's hands is the sense of freeing.
branches.cn: 把重物从某人手里拿走，就是使其摆脱。

branches.en: A dull stretch is pressure too, so a change relieves it.
branches.cn: 沉闷的时段也是一种压力，变化正是在缓解它。

branches.en: All three come from the same movement of weight leaving a person.
branches.cn: 前三项都来自重量离开同一个人的同一个动作。

intro.en: Relieve keeps the Latin prefix, the Latin root, and a French verb ending in one short word.
intro.cn: relieve 在短短一个词里保留了拉丁前缀、拉丁词根和法语动词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin re- adds the idea of back or again, and levare supplies the lifting, so the verb means to lift back up.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁前缀 re- 带来「回、再」的意思，levare 提供「举起」，合起来就是「重新抬起」。

items.example: Re- appears again in remove and renew.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 re- 也出现在 remove 与 renew 中。

items.example: The lev- root also lifts in lever.
items.exampleCN: lev- 词根在 lever 中也表示抬起。

items.example: Levare supplies the second half of relieve.
items.exampleCN: levare 提供 relieve 的后半部分。

items.meaningCN: 标记动词不定式形式的词尾
items.example: The final -e comes from the French infinitive relever.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -e 来自法语不定式 relever。

items.example: Relevare is the direct ancestor of relever.
items.exampleCN: relevare 是 relever 的直接来源。

items.meaning: the easing of pain or worry
items.example: Relief drops the verb ending and keeps the same root.
items.exampleCN: relief 去掉动词词尾，保留同一词根。

items.meaning: a bar used to lift or move something
items.example: Lever is the lev- root in its plainest lifting form.
items.exampleCN: lever 是 lev- 词根最直白的「抬起」形式。

items.meaning: to raise to a higher position
items.example: Elevate adds e- to the same lev- root.
items.exampleCN: elevate 在同一个 lev- 词根前加了 e-。

definition_zh: 确保；保证；使必然发生
definition_en: to make certain that something happens or is true
core_image: 用手把门闩牢牢扣上，让事情没有出岔子的余地
scene: 出发前她把清单又核对了一遍，确认每件行李都上了车。 She checked the list again to ensure that every bag was on the bus.
sceneCN: 这里 ensure 是「确保」（第 1 个义项：使某事必然发生）；句意：她又核对了一遍清单，以确保每件行李都上了车。

senses.title: To make certain an outcome
senses.definition: to take action so that something certainly happens
senses.definitionCN: 采取行动，使某事确定发生
senses.example: Please ensure that the door is locked before you leave.
senses.exampleCN: 离开前请确保门已锁好。
senses.why: The word is built on sure, so the verb literally means to make an outcome sure.
senses.whyCN: 这个词建立在 sure 之上，因此动词字面上就是「使结果确定」。

senses.title: To protect or guarantee
senses.definition: to make a person or right safe from harm or unfair treatment
senses.definitionCN: 使某人或某项权利免受伤害或不公平对待
senses.example: The new rules ensure fair treatment for all workers.
senses.exampleCN: 新规定保障所有工人得到公平对待。
senses.why: Protecting people is the same certainty applied to their safety and rights.
senses.whyCN: 保护人，就是把同样的「确定」用于他们的安全与权利。

senses.title: To secure a result in advance
senses.definition: to arrange conditions so that a desired result can be secured
senses.definitionCN: 事先安排好条件，使期望的结果有把握到来
senses.example: Hard work does not ensure success, but it improves the chances.
senses.exampleCN: 努力不能确保成功，但能提高成功的可能。
senses.why: Here the word points to securing the way things turn out, not to a legal promise.
senses.whyCN: 这里指把事情的走向「锁定」，而不是法律意义上的承诺。

intro.en: Ensure comes from Anglo-Norman enseurer, from Old French asseürer, to assure, built on Latin securus, free from care.
intro.cn: ensure 来自盎格鲁-诺曼语 enseurer，源于古法语 asseürer（使确信），建立在拉丁语 securus（无忧的）之上。

items.en: Securus means free from care, from se-, apart, and cura, care.
items.cn: securus 意为无忧的，由 se-（脱离）与 cura（忧虑）构成。

items.en: Assecurare means to make safe or free from worry.
items.cn: assecurare 意为使安全、使无忧。

items.en: Asseürer carries the meaning to assure or make certain.
items.cn: asseürer 意为使确信、使有保证。

items.en: Enseurer develops the en- form used in English law and trade.
items.cn: enseurer 发展出英语法律与商业中使用的 en- 形式。

items.en: Middle English ensuren means to make safe or certain.
items.cn: 中古英语 ensuren 意为使安全或使确定。

items.en: Modern English uses ensure mainly for making an outcome certain.
items.cn: 现代英语中，ensure 主要用于表示「使结果确定」。

note.en: Ensure belongs to the sure family, and it sits near verbs for guaranteeing and securing.
note.cn: ensure 属于「确定」词族，与表示保证和确保的动词相邻。

entries.definition: to protect against loss with an insurance policy
entries.definitionCN: 给……保险

entries.definition: to tell someone confidently that something is true
entries.definitionCN: 向……保证

entries.definition: a confident promise or belief
entries.definitionCN: 保证；信心

entries.definition: to promise that something will certainly happen
entries.definitionCN: 保证；担保

entries.definition: to make something safe or certain
entries.definitionCN: 使安全；确保

entries.definition: to make a fact or arrangement certain
entries.definitionCN: 确认；证实

normalIntro.en: Ensure contains sure: the whole point of the verb is to make an outcome sure.
normalIntro.cn: ensure 含有 sure：这个动词的全部要点就是让结果「确定」。

normal.en: En- turns the adjective sure into a verb meaning make sure.
normal.cn: 前缀 en- 把形容词 sure 变成动词，意为「使确定」。

normal.en: Ensure that is the most common pattern, and it is followed by a full clause.
normal.cn: ensure that 是最常见的搭配，后面接完整从句。

normal.en: Keep ensure and insure apart: one makes certain, the other buys insurance.
normal.cn: 把 ensure 与 insure 分开：一个表示使确定，另一个表示买保险。

normal.en: Compare assure: assure works on people, while ensure works on outcomes.
normal.cn: 对比 assure：assure 的对象是人，ensure 的对象是结果。

normal.en: In formal writing, ensure often replaces make sure.
normal.cn: 在正式写作中，ensure 常用来替代 make sure。

abstract.en: Picture a latch clicked shut, so the door cannot swing open in the night.
abstract.cn: 想象门闩咔嗒扣上，夜里门再也吹不开。

abstract.en: Imagine checking every seat belt before the bus leaves.
abstract.cn: 想象大巴出发前逐条检查安全带。

abstract.en: Think of a knot pulled tight so the load cannot slip.
abstract.cn: 想象绳结被拉紧，货物不会滑脱。

examples.en: The nurse ensured that the patient was comfortable.
examples.cn: 护士确保病人躺得舒服。

examples.en: Regular checks ensure the machines run safely.
examples.cn: 定期检查确保机器安全运转。

examples.en: To ensure a seat, book your ticket early.
examples.cn: 想确保有座位，就早点订票。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因 sure」——因为确定，所以 ensure 就是确保；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 securus（无忧的）→ 俗拉丁语 assecurare（使安全）→ 古法语 asseürer → 盎格鲁-诺曼语 enseurer → 中古英语 ensuren → 现代英语 ensure，核心义「使确定无疑」。

sensesIntro.en: The word moves from freedom from care to the act of making an outcome certain, then to legal and practical guarantees.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从「无忧」出发，转到「使结果确定」的动作，再延伸到法律与实际层面的保障。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a latch fastened so that the outcome cannot slip away.
core.cn: 核心意象：门闩扣紧，结果无法溜走。

branches.en: Making an outcome certain is the everyday core sense.
branches.cn: 使结果确定，是日常的核心义项。

branches.en: Protecting people or rights extends the same certainty into safety.
branches.cn: 保护人或权利，把同样的确定延伸到安全。

branches.en: Securing a result means arranging the conditions in advance.
branches.cn: 确保得到结果，就是事先安排条件。

branches.en: Certainty and safety are two sides of the same promise.
branches.cn: 确定与安全是同一个承诺的两面。

branches.en: Protection and advance planning often appear together in rules.
branches.cn: 保护与事前规划常一起出现在规则里。

intro.en: Ensure is a French-shaped verb with a Latin core, and its small family grows with English endings.
intro.cn: ensure 是法语形态的动词，核心来自拉丁语，其小词族由英语词尾扩展。

latinIntro.en: Latin cura means care, securus means free from care, and assecurare means to make safe.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 cura 表示忧虑，securus 表示无忧，assecurare 表示使安全。

items.exampleCN: en- 出现在 ensure 与 enlarge 开头。

items.example: Securus is the deep root behind ensure.
items.exampleCN: securus 是 ensure 背后的深层词根。

items.example: Se- in securus means apart from care.
items.exampleCN: securus 中的 se- 意为脱离忧虑。

items.example: Cura supplies the idea of care.
items.exampleCN: cura 提供「关心、忧虑」的意思。
assecurare 把两部分连接起来。

items.example: Asseürer carries the verb into French.
items.exampleCN: asseürer 把这个动词带入法语。

items.example: Enseurer gives English its en- form.
items.exampleCN: enseurer 为英语提供 en- 形式。

items.meaningCN: 表示动作或状态的名词词尾

items.example: Ensurance is now archaic or rare.
items.exampleCN: ensurance 现在已古旧或罕见。

definition_zh: 提及；参考；参考文献；推荐信；参照物；（计算机）引用
definition_en: a mention of something, a source consulted, or a point against which something else is judged
core_image: 书桌上摊开一本厚词典，页边贴着写有编号的便签
scene: 写论文的时候，老师反复叮嘱：每一条说法都要交代出处。 The article makes frequent reference to earlier studies of the same topic.
sceneCN: 这里 reference 指「提及」（第 1 个义项：在言语或文字中说到某事物）；句意：这篇文章频繁提及对同一湖泊的早期研究。图中可辨识物件：打开的书、编号便签、书签、引用标记。

pos.zh: 提及；参考；参考文献；推荐信；参照物；查询
引用；参考（多用于学术与技术文本）

senses.title: A mention
senses.titleCN: 提及：在话语或文字中说到某事物
senses.definition: an act of mentioning someone or something in speech or writing
senses.definitionCN: 在口头或书面中说到某人或某事物的行为
senses.example: The article makes frequent reference to earlier studies.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章频繁提及早期的研究。
senses.why: Reference comes from referre 'to carry back', and a mention carries the reader's mind back to the thing named.
senses.whyCN: reference 出自 referre「带回」，而一次提及正是把读者的心思带回被命名的事物。

senses.title: A cited source
senses.titleCN: 参考文献：被引用的出处
senses.definition: a source cited in a text, or the entry that identifies it
senses.definitionCN: 正文所引用的出处，或标识该出处的条目
senses.example: Every claim in the paper has a reference at the end of the sentence.
senses.exampleCN: 论文中每一处主张在句末都有参考文献。
senses.why: The same carrying-back motion now points at a document: the text sends the reader to the place where the claim came from.
senses.whyCN: 同一个「带回」动作现在指向文件：正文把读者送回主张的来源之处。

senses.title: A reference work
senses.titleCN: 工具书：供查阅而非通读的书
senses.definition: a book or database consulted for specific facts rather than read through
senses.definitionCN: 为查具体事实而查阅、而非从头读到尾的书或数据库
senses.example: The librarian keeps the dictionaries and atlases in the reference section.
senses.exampleCN: 图书管理员把词典与地图集放在参考区。
senses.why: Here the noun has become a label for a class of books whose purpose is to be referred to.
senses.whyCN: 这里名词已成为一类书籍的标签，这类书的存在就是为了被查阅。

senses.title: A recommendation
senses.titleCN: 推荐信：为求职者作证的文件
senses.definition: a letter or statement in which someone speaks in support of an applicant
senses.definitionCN: 某人为申请人提供支持的书面陈述或信件
senses.example: She asked her former manager for a reference.
senses.exampleCN: 她请前任经理写一封推荐信。
senses.why: The recommender 'refers' the employer back to facts about the candidate, so the letter is called a reference.
senses.whyCN: 推荐人把雇主「引回」候选人的事实，因此这封信叫 reference。

senses.title: A basis for comparison
senses.titleCN: 参照物：用来比较的基准
senses.definition: a standard, point or system against which other things are measured or understood
senses.definitionCN: 用于衡量或理解其他事物的标准、点或系统
senses.example: The fixed stars provided a reference for early navigators.
senses.exampleCN: 恒星为早期航海者提供了参照。
senses.why: To refer is to send something back to a fixed point; a reference point is exactly that anchor.
senses.whyCN: refer 就是把某物送回一个固定点；reference point 正是这样的锚点。

senses.title: A computing reference
senses.titleCN: 计算机引用：指向对象或地址的间接名称
senses.definition: in computing, a value that points to an object or memory location rather than holding the data itself
senses.definitionCN: 计算机中指向对象或内存位置、而非直接保存数据的值
senses.example: The function returns a reference to the cached record.
senses.exampleCN: 该函数返回对缓存记录的引用。
senses.why: Programming borrowed the everyday idea of pointing back: a reference lets the program reach the original object without copying it.
senses.whyCN: 编程借用了「指回」的日常观念：引用让程序无需复制就能抵达原对象。

senses.title: A linguistic referent
senses.titleCN: 语言指称：词语所指的对象
senses.definition: in linguistics, the object or entity in the world that a word or phrase points to
senses.definitionCN: 语言学中词语或短语所指向的现实对象或实体
senses.example: The reference of 'the mayor' depends on who holds office.
senses.exampleCN: 「市长」一词的指称取决于谁在任。
senses.why: Linguists separated the word from the thing: the expression refers, and its reference is the thing it reaches.
senses.whyCN: 语言学家把词与物分开：表达式进行指称，而它的 reference 就是所抵达之物。

senses.title: An employment inquiry
senses.titleCN: 背景查询：向原单位核实情况
senses.definition: an inquiry made to a previous employer or institution about a person's record
senses.definitionCN: 向原雇主或机构核实某人履历的查询
senses.example: The hiring manager made a reference call before the offer.
senses.exampleCN: 发出录用通知前，招聘经理打了背景核实电话。
senses.why: The HR sense extends the document sense into a process: someone is asked to refer the new employer back to the record.
senses.whyCN: 人事义把文件义扩展为过程：有人被请求把新雇主引回履历记录。

intro.en: Reference comes from Latin referre 'to carry back', built on ferre 'to bear, carry'. English took the noun through French and Medieval Latin forms, and the modern senses range from mention to citation.
intro.cn: reference 出自拉丁 referre「带回」，基于 ferre「携带、承受」。英语经由法语与中世纪拉丁形式取得该名词，现代义从「提及」一直延伸到「引用」。

items.en: Latin ferre meant 'to bear, carry, bring'. Its compounds include transfer, offer, infer, refer and prefer, each with a different prefix direction.
items.cn: 拉丁 ferre 意为「携带、运送、带来」，其复合词包括 transfer、offer、infer、refer、prefer，各前缀设定不同方向。

items.en: Referre joined re- 'back' to ferre, meaning 'to carry back, bring back, direct to'. It could refer a question to a person or a matter to a source.
items.cn: referre 把 re-「回」加到 ferre，意为「带回、拿回、指向」，可用于把问题交给某人，或把事项指向某来源。

items.en: Medieval Latin referentia and French reference supplied the noun 'a referring, a relation'. The exact route into English is uncertain in detail.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁 referentia 与法语 reference 提供了「指涉、关联」的名词。进入英语的确切路径细节存疑。

items.en: English reference developed from 'relation or respect' to 'a mention', then to 'a cited source' and 'a recommendation'.
items.cn: 英语 reference 从「关联、方面」发展为「提及」，再发展为「被引出处」与「推荐」。

items.en: Computing added the pointer sense in the twentieth century, while linguistics fixed reference as the relation between expression and object.
items.cn: 20 世纪计算机领域增加了「指针」义，语言学则把 reference 固定为表达式与对象之间的关系。

items.en: The precise first English date is uncertain, and the deeper origin of ferre is discussed only as a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词根与传入路径）：英语最早书证确切年代存疑；ferre 的更深来源只作为重构来讨论。

note.en: The first group separates the refer family; the second gives near-synonyms for mentioning, citing or a standard of comparison.
note.cn: 第一组区分 refer 词族；第二组给出关于提及、引用或比较基准的近义词。

entries.definition: To mention, consult or direct someone to something. The noun reference names the mention or the source.
entries.definitionCN: 指提及、查阅或把某人引向某物；名词 reference 命名该提及或出处。

entries.definition: A sports official or a person who writes a recommendation. A referee is a person; a reference may be a document.
entries.definitionCN: 指体育裁判或写推荐的人。referee 是人，reference 可以是文件。

entries.definition: The act of sending someone to another doctor or service. It is the transfer, not the cited source.
entries.definitionCN: 指把某人转给另一位医生或服务；是转介行为，不是被引出处。

entries.definition: In linguistics, the actual object a word points to. Reference is the relation; the referent is the target.
entries.definitionCN: 语言学中词语指向的实际对象。reference 是关系，referent 是目标。

entries.definition: A formal quotation of a source with identifying details. It is narrower than reference, which can also mean a mere mention.
entries.definitionCN: 指带识别信息的正式引用；比 reference 窄，后者也可仅指提及。

entries.definition: An indirect or passing mention meant to be recognized. It does not provide a source.
entries.definitionCN: 指有意让人识别出的间接或顺带提及，不提供出处。

entries.definition: A rule or measure used for comparison. A reference point anchors measurement; a standard defines what counts as acceptable.
entries.definitionCN: 指用于比较的规则或尺度。参照点用于锚定测量；标准则界定何为合格。

entries.definition: The origin of information or material. A reference identifies a source, but the source is the thing itself.
entries.definitionCN: 指信息或材料的来源。reference 标识出处，而 source 是那个来源本身。

entries.definition: A written statement praising a person's qualities, often for employment. It overlaps sense 4 but stresses praise.
entries.definitionCN: 指称赞某人品质的书面陈述，常用于求职；与第 4 个义项重叠，但更强调赞扬。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: re- 'back' + ferre 'carry' + -ence: carrying the mind back to a source.
normal.cn: re-「回」+ ferre「携带」+ -ence：把心思带回某个来源。

normal.en: The family runs refer, referee, referral, referendum, referential.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 refer、referee、referral、referendum、referential。

normal.en: Fixed phrases show the senses: with reference to, reference book, frame of reference, letter of reference.
normal.cn: 固定搭配展示义项：关于、工具书、参照系、推荐信。

normal.en: A reference points back; a referent is the thing pointed at.
normal.cn: reference 指回，referent 是被指的东西。

normal.en: citation is formal quoting; allusion is indirect mention without a source.
normal.cn: citation 是正式引用；allusion 是不给出处的间接提及。

abstract.en: Picture a bookmark that sends your finger back to one exact page.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚书签把你的手指送回确切的一页。

abstract.en: Picture a surveyor's pole standing fixed while everything else is measured against it.
abstract.cn: 想象测量员的标杆固定不动，其余一切都以它为基准。

abstract.en: Picture a thread tied from a note to the drawer where its evidence is kept.
abstract.cn: 想象一根线把便条连到存放证据的抽屉。

examples.en: The report makes no reference to the earlier failed trial.
examples.cn: 这份报告只字未提早先那次失败的试验。

examples.en: Keep a reference list in the same style throughout the thesis.
examples.cn: 整篇论文的参考文献表要保持同一体例。

examples.en: The compass needle needs a fixed reference to show direction.
examples.cn: 罗盘指针需要一个固定参照才能显示方向。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「re（回）+ fer（带）」——把话头带回原处 → reference 提及、参考

root: 拉丁 ferre「携带」→ referre「带回、指向」→ 中世纪拉丁 referentia；英语 reference。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all point back: a mention points to a topic, a citation to a source, a reference book to facts, a letter to a record, a point to a scale, a variable to an object, a word to a referent, a call to an employer.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在「指回」：提及指向话题，引用指向出处，工具书指向事实，推荐信指向履历，参照点指向尺度，变量指向对象，词语指向指称物，核实电话指向雇主。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bookmark sending the finger back to one exact page.
core.cn: 核心意象：书签把手指送回确切的一页。

branches.en: TEXTUAL POINTING: a mention in prose, and the cited source that backs it.
branches.cn: 文本指涉：文中的提及，以及支撑它的被引出处。

branches.en: DOCUMENTS: a book made for consultation, or a letter that points an employer to a record.
branches.cn: 文件：为查阅而作的书，或把雇主引向履历的信。

branches.en: MEASUREMENT: a fixed point or frame against which things are judged.
branches.cn: 测量：用于判断事物的固定点或框架。

branches.en: SYMBOLIC POINTING: a program value or a word reaches an object without being that object.
branches.cn: 符号指涉：程序值或词语抵达对象，却不等于对象本身。

branches.en: PROCEDURE: the document sense becomes a call that checks a record.
branches.cn: 程序：文件义变成核实履历的一通电话。

intro.en: Reference is a Latin verb of carrying plus a noun ending: re- 'back' + ferre 'carry' + -ence. The same root appears across a large family of English verbs of transfer.
intro.cn: reference 是拉丁「携带」动词加名词词尾：re-「回」+ ferre「携带」+ -ence。同一词根出现在大量英语「转移」动词中。

latinIntro.en: The ferre family includes refer, transfer, offer, infer, prefer, confer, differ and suffer; the shared image is bearing something from one place or person to another.
latinIntro.cn: ferre 词族包括 refer、transfer、offer、infer、prefer、confer、differ、suffer；共同意象是把某物从一处或一人带到另一处或另一人。

items.meaning: a pointing back; a mention or source
items.example: The book contains useful references to primary sources.
items.exampleCN: 这本书含有指向原始资料的有用参考。

items.meaning: one to whom a matter is referred; an official
the act of sending someone onward
items.meaningCN: 把某人转介出去的行为
items.example: The doctor wrote a referral to a specialist.
items.exampleCN: 医生写了转诊单给专科医生。

items.structure: Latin referendum (that which must be referred)
items.meaning: a vote referred to the people
items.example: The constitution was changed by referendum.
items.exampleCN: 宪法通过全民公投得以修改。

items.example: The files were transferred to a new server.
items.exampleCN: 文件被转移到新服务器。

items.meaning: to carry a conclusion into view
items.example: We inferred the cause from the pattern.
items.exampleCN: 我们从模式推断出原因。

items.meaning: to carry before others; to favour
items.exampleCN: 她更喜欢茶而不是咖啡。

definition_en: sliced bread browned by heat, a call to drink in someone's honour, or to brown bread and to drink in honour

scene: 清晨厨房里飘出焦香味。 She buttered a slice of hot toast.
sceneCN: 这里 toast 是「烤面包片」（第 1 个义项：烤黄的面包）；句意：她给一片热吐司抹上黄油。

senses.title: Brown bread from heat
senses.definition: bread made crisp and brown by heating
senses.definitionCN: 经烘烤变得焦黄酥脆的面包
senses.example: Breakfast was eggs and toast.
senses.exampleCN: 早餐是鸡蛋和吐司。
senses.why: The core image is pale bread turned golden by fire.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是苍白面包被火烤成金黄。

senses.title: To brown bread by heat
senses.definition: to make bread, cheese or nuts crisp by heating them
senses.definitionCN: 把面包、奶酪或坚果烤脆
senses.example: Toast the almonds in a dry pan.
senses.exampleCN: 用干锅把杏仁烤香。
senses.why: The thing made becomes the verb that makes it.
senses.whyCN: 制成物变回制造它的动词。

senses.title: A drink in someone's honour
senses.definition: an act of raising glasses and drinking to honour a person or event
senses.definitionCN: 举杯向某人或某事致敬的饮酒行为
senses.example: They raised their glasses in a toast to the couple.
senses.exampleCN: 他们举杯向新人敬酒。
senses.why: The honoured name is dropped into the wine like spice into warmed drink.
senses.whyCN: 被致敬的名字落进酒里，如香料落入温酒。

senses.title: The words spoken at a toast
senses.definition: a short speech or sentence said while raising a glass
senses.definitionCN: 举杯时说的简短祝语
senses.example: His toast made everyone laugh.
senses.exampleCN: 他的祝词让大家都笑了。
senses.why: The act of honouring extends to the words that carry it.
senses.whyCN: 致敬之举延伸为承载它的言辞。

senses.title: To drink in honour of someone
senses.definition: to honour a person by raising glasses and drinking
senses.definitionCN: 以举杯饮酒的方式向某人致敬
senses.example: The team toasted their coach after the final.
senses.exampleCN: 决赛后全队向教练敬酒。
senses.why: The noun of the act becomes the act itself.
senses.whyCN: 行为的名词变成行为本身。

senses.title: A person honoured by many
senses.definition: a person widely celebrated, as in the toast of the town
senses.definitionCN: 广受赞誉的人，如 the toast of the town
senses.example: Overnight the young singer became the toast of the town.
senses.exampleCN: 一夜之间，年轻歌手成了全城的宠儿。
senses.why: Many glasses raised to one name make the person the drink's purpose.
senses.whyCN: 众多酒杯为同一个名字举起，此人便成了酒的意义。

senses.title: Warm as toast: warmed through
senses.definition: informal for comfortably warm, as near a fire
senses.definitionCN: 口语中指暖和舒适，如在火边
senses.example: By the stove we were as warm as toast.
senses.exampleCN: 在炉边我们暖烘烘的。
senses.why: The fire that browns bread also warms people.
senses.whyCN: 烤黄面包的火同样温暖人。

senses.title: Toasted: condemned or finished
senses.definition: informal for someone or something doomed, or harshly criticized
senses.definitionCN: 口语中指注定失败或遭严厉批评
senses.example: Without the data, the project is toast.
senses.exampleCN: 没有数据，项目就完蛋了。
senses.why: What the fire takes is gone; the burnt state became slang for ruin.
senses.whyCN: 被火夺走的便不复存在；焦糊态成了完蛋的俚语。

intro.en: Toast comes from Old French toster, to roast, from Latin tostare, a frequentative of torrere, to parch. The drinking sense grew from spiced bread dropped into warm wine at feasts.
intro.cn: toast 出自古法语 toster「烘烤」，源自拉丁语 torrere 的反复动词 tostare「烤干」。饮酒义源于宴会上把香料面包投入温酒的做法。

items.en: Torrere meant to parch and dry with heat.
items.cn: 拉丁语 torrere 意为用热力烤干。

items.en: Toster kept the sense of roasting before a fire.
items.cn: 古法语 toster 保留在火前烘烤之义。

items.en: Toast named the browned slice of bread.
items.cn: 中古英语 toast 指烤黄的面包片。

items.en: Spiced toast was floated in warm wine at banquets.
items.cn: 十五世纪宴会上把香料吐司浸入温酒。

items.en: A celebrated lady was likened to the flavouring toast, giving the drinking sense.
items.cn: 十七世纪把受赞美的女士比作酒中的调味吐司，产生敬酒义。

items.en: Modern usage keeps bread, fire, honour and slang for ruin.
items.cn: 现代用法兼有面包、火、致敬与完蛋的俚语。

note.en: The first group gathers look-alike -oast words; the second sorts honour-and-heat neighbours.
note.cn: 第一组是 -oast 形近词；第二组列出致敬与受热义的近邻。

entries.definition: to cook with dry heat, especially meat
entries.definitionCN: 烤（肉）；与 toast 同源

entries.definition: the land beside the sea
entries.definitionCN: 海岸；拼写相近而非同词

entries.definition: to talk with too much pride
entries.definitionCN: 自夸

entries.definition: a friendly word said while raising glasses
entries.definitionCN: 干杯时的招呼语

entries.definition: to cook bread or cakes in an oven
entries.definitionCN: 烘；焙

entries.definition: to greet or honour someone formally
entries.definitionCN: 致意；敬礼

normalIntro.en: Real links: hot toast, propose a toast, warm as toast, and the project is toast.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：热吐司、提议举杯、暖烘烘，以及项目完蛋了。

normal.en: Toast is bread turned golden by fire.
normal.cn: toast 是被火烤成金黄的面包。

normal.en: A toast drops a name into the wine.
normal.cn: 敬酒是把一个名字落进酒里。

normal.en: Warm as toast borrows the heat of the hearth.
normal.cn: warm as toast 借用了炉火的热。

normal.en: The singer became the toast of the town.
normal.cn: 歌手成了全城举杯致敬的人。

normal.en: If the project is toast, the fire has won.
normal.cn: 若项目完蛋，那就是火赢了。

abstract.en: Every toast is heat marking a change of state.
abstract.cn: 每个 toast 都是热力标记的状态改变。

abstract.en: Honour, like spice, is dropped into the cup.
abstract.cn: 敬意如香料，被投进杯中。

abstract.en: What fire finishes, language calls toast.
abstract.cn: 被火终结之物，语言称之为 toast。

examples.en: She dropped two slices of bread into the toaster.
examples.cn: 她把两片面包放进烤面包机。

examples.en: The captain gave a toast to the crew.
examples.cn: 船长向全体船员敬酒。

examples.en: Toast the nuts until they smell sweet.
examples.cn: 把坚果烤到散发出香味。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「吐司」——toast 的音译本尊，烤黄的面包片 → toast 吐司；祝酒

root: 单一词干：拉丁语 torrere「烤干」的反复式 tostare，经古法语 toster 进入英语。核心意象是热力使物焦黄；饮酒义由浸酒的香料吐司引申。

sensesIntro.en: Toast browns bread, warms rooms, and raises honoured names in wine.
sensesIntro.cn: toast 烤黄面包、温暖房间，也把受敬的名字举进酒杯。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: fire turning pale things golden, and names dropped into raised glasses.
core.cn: 核心意象：火把苍白之物烤成金黄，名字落入举起的酒杯。

branches.en: Bread, browning and borrowed warmth.
branches.cn: 面包、烤制与借来的温暖。

branches.en: Raising glasses, words and the act itself.
branches.cn: 举杯、祝词与敬酒之举。

branches.en: The person everyone drinks to.
branches.cn: 众人为之举杯的人。

branches.en: Slang: finished by the fire.
branches.cn: 俚语：被火终结。

branches.en: The wine custom that links bread and honour.
branches.cn: 连接面包与敬意的酒俗。

intro.en: Toast is a Latin stem through French; its items show agent nouns and warm compounds.
intro.cn: toast 是经法语传入的拉丁词干；条目展示施动名词与温暖的复合词。

latinIntro.en: Latin torrere also gives torrid, scorch and roast family words.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 torrere 还派生 torrid（炎热的）与 roast 一族。

items.meaning: a machine for browning bread; one who proposes toasts
items.example: The toaster popped up two slices.
items.exampleCN: 烤面包机弹出两片吐司。

items.example: The room felt toasty by evening.

items.meaning: bread dipped in egg and fried
items.example: We had French toast and syrup.
items.exampleCN: 我们吃了法式吐司配糖浆。

items.example: Melt the cheese in the toaster oven.

items.meaning: to cook with dry heat; meat so cooked
items.example: They roast a chicken every Sunday.
The torrid summer dried the fields.

items.meaning: the official who proposes toasts at formal dinners

definition_zh: 委员会；理事会；地方议会；会议
definition_en: a group of people chosen to make decisions or give advice, especially for a town or organisation
core_image: 一张圆桌旁围坐着被推选出来的人，举手决定一件事
scene: 会议室里十二个人围坐一圈，举手表决是否修那条路。 The city council voted to repair the old road.
sceneCN: 这里 council 指「地方议会」（第 2 个义项：管理城镇事务的议事机构）；句意是市议会投票决定修那条旧路。

pos.zh: 委员会；理事会；地方议会；会议

senses.title: A chosen decision group
senses.definition: a group of people chosen to make decisions or give advice
senses.definitionCN: 被推选出来做决定或提建议的一群人
senses.example: The arts council gave the theatre a grant.
senses.exampleCN: 艺术委员会给了这家剧院一笔拨款。
senses.why: Many voices need one table to become one decision.
senses.whyCN: 许多声音需要一张桌子，才能变成一个决定。

senses.title: The body that runs a town
senses.definition: the group that governs a town or local area
senses.definitionCN: 管理一座城镇或地方区域的机构
senses.example: The city council voted to repair the old road.
senses.exampleCN: 市议会投票决定修那条旧路。
senses.why: A town is too large for one desk, so it borrows a table of many.
senses.whyCN: 一座城一张桌子管不过来，于是借来一张多人的桌子。

senses.title: A meeting for advice
senses.definition: a formal meeting held to discuss and advise on a matter
senses.definitionCN: 为讨论并议定某事而召开的正式会议
senses.example: The generals held a council before dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 将军们在黎明前开了一次军事会议。
senses.why: Before a hard act comes a room where words are weighed.
senses.whyCN: 艰难行动之前，总有一间称量话语的屋子。

intro.en: Council comes from Latin concilium, a calling together, from com-, together, and calare, to call.
intro.cn: council 来自拉丁语 concilium（召集到一起），由 com-（一起）与 calare（呼喊、召集）构成。

items.en: Calare meant to call or summon.
items.cn: calare 意为呼喊或召集。

items.en: Concilium named a body called together for advice.
items.cn: concilium 指为商议而被召集起来的团体。

items.en: Concile meant an assembly or a meeting.
items.cn: concile 意为集会或会议。

items.en: English council named a group that advises a ruler.
items.cn: 英语 council 指为统治者出主意的团体。

items.en: It now names town bodies, committees and formal meetings.
items.cn: 今天它指市政机构、委员会与正式会议。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the easily confused council, counsel and consul, and the meaning group names other decision groups.
note.cn: 形近组收集易混的 council、counsel 与 consul，近义组列出其他决策团体。

entries.definition: advice, or a lawyer who gives it
entries.definitionCN: 建议，或提供建议的律师

entries.definition: an official living abroad to help citizens
entries.definitionCN: 驻外帮助本国公民的官员

entries.definition: to comfort someone in sadness
entries.definitionCN: 在悲伤中安慰某人

entries.definition: a small group chosen for a special task
entries.definitionCN: 为专项任务选出的少数人

entries.definition: the group that directs a company
entries.definitionCN: 领导一家公司的团体

entries.definition: a group gathered for a shared purpose
entries.definitionCN: 为共同目的聚集的群体

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a round table of chosen people, then move to a town body and to generals meeting before dawn.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从被推选者的圆桌开始，再到市政机构，最后到黎明前开会的将军们。

normal.en: Council hides the word call: people called together to decide.
normal.cn: council 里藏着 call：被叫到一起做决定的人。

normal.en: Council is the group; counsel is the advice it gives.
normal.cn: council 是团体，counsel 是它给出的建议。

normal.en: A council sits at a round table so no seat looks highest.
normal.cn: 议会坐圆桌，这样没有哪个座位显得最高。

normal.en: City council decides roads, housing and rubbish.
normal.cn: 市议会决定道路、住房与垃圾的事。

normal.en: The ending -il is quiet, but the word means loud debate.
normal.cn: 词尾 -il 很安静，这个词的意思却是喧闹的辩论。

abstract.en: Picture many hands rising in a single room.
abstract.cn: 想象许多只手在同一间屋子里举起。

abstract.en: Picture a round table worn smooth by elbows.
abstract.cn: 想象一张被手肘磨得光滑的圆桌。

abstract.en: Picture a town seen from above as many doors and one table.
abstract.cn: 想象从高处看一座城，许多扇门和一张桌子。

examples.en: The city council voted to repair the old road.
examples.cn: 市议会投票决定修那条旧路。

examples.en: The arts council gave the theatre a grant.
examples.cn: 艺术委员会给了这家剧院一笔拨款。

examples.en: The generals held a council before dawn.
examples.cn: 将军们在黎明前开了一次军事会议。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 council 记成「被 call 到一起的人」：被召集来议事的团体，就是委员会与议会。

root: 源自拉丁语 concilium（集会），由 com-（一起）与 calare（呼喊、召集）构成，本指被召集议事的人，后指委员会与地方议会。

sensesIntro.en: From a group called to advise, to the body that runs a town, and at last to the meeting itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 从被召来出主意的团体，到管理城镇的机构，最后到会议本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: chosen people seated around one round table.
core.cn: 核心意象：被推选的人围坐在一张圆桌旁。

branches.en: A chosen group turns talk into advice.
branches.cn: 被选出的团体把谈话变成建议。

branches.en: A town body turns advice into local rules.
branches.cn: 市政机构把建议变成地方规矩。

branches.en: A meeting turns many voices into one plan.
branches.cn: 一场会议把许多声音变成一个方案。

branches.en: Both are bodies with the power to decide.
branches.cn: 两者都是握有决定权的机构。

branches.en: The body and its meeting share one name because the meeting is the body at work.
branches.cn: 机构与会议共用一个名字，因为会议就是机构在工作。

intro.en: Council rests on Latin calare, to call, with com-, together, and the noun shape -ium.
intro.cn: council 建立在拉丁语 calare（呼喊、召集）之上，配 com-（一起）与名词形态 -ium。

latinIntro.en: The calling base cal- also appears in calendar and clamour.
latinIntro.cn: 表示呼喊与召集的词基 cal- 也出现在 calendar 与 clamour 中。

items.example: The councilwoman asked for a vote.

homes owned by a local council

items.exampleCN: 他们在市政住房里长大。

definition_zh: 禁止；禁令
definition_en: to officially forbid something, or an official order that forbids it
core_image: 门口立起一块写有禁止字样的木牌
scene: 公告贴在体育馆门口。 The city decided to ban smoking in parks.
sceneCN: 这里 ban 是「禁止」（第 1 个义项：官方明令不许做某事）；句意是市里决定禁止在公园吸烟。

derivatives.zh: 由 ban 加 -ned 构成，义为「被禁止的」
由 ban 加 -ning 构成，义为「禁止的行为」
同源词，来自古法语 banir，义为「放逐」

senses.title: To forbid officially
senses.definition: to officially say that something must not be done
senses.definitionCN: 官方宣布某事不许做
senses.example: The city decided to ban smoking in parks.
senses.exampleCN: 市里决定禁止在公园吸烟。
senses.why: Ban began as a word for a public proclamation, and an order that forbids something is the modern use.
senses.whyCN: ban 起初指公开宣告，而宣布禁止某事就是它如今的用法。

senses.title: An official order
senses.definition: an official rule that forbids something
senses.definitionCN: 官方禁止某事的规则
senses.example: The government lifted the ban on travel.
senses.exampleCN: 政府解除了旅行禁令。
senses.why: The noun names the proclamation itself, so a ban is the written or announced order.
senses.whyCN: 名词指的是宣告本身，所以 ban 就是那份明令。

intro.en: Ban is an old word for a public proclamation.
intro.cn: ban 是表示「公开宣告」的古词。

items.en: bannan meant 'to summon or proclaim'.
items.cn: bannan 意为「召集或宣告」。

items.en: bannum meant 'a proclamation'.
items.cn: bannum 意为「公告」。

items.en: ban meant 'a public order'.
items.cn: ban 意为「公开的命令」。

items.en: ban narrowed to an official prohibition.
items.cn: ban 缩小为官方的禁止。

items.en: ban is common in law and sport.
items.cn: 如今 ban 常见于法律与体育。

note.en: The look-alike group differs by one vowel; the near-meaning group gives stronger legal words.
note.cn: 形近组只差一个元音；近义组是更强的法律用语。

entries.definitionCN: 依法禁止

normalIntro.en: A ban is an official stop sign.
normalIntro.cn: ban 是一块官方的停止牌。

normal.en: The past tense is banned, with double n.
normal.cn: 过去式是 banned，双写 n。

normal.en: A ban on something uses the preposition on.
normal.cn: a ban on 后接被禁的事物。

normal.en: Lift a ban means end it.
normal.cn: lift a ban 意为解除禁令。

normal.en: Impose a ban means start it.
normal.cn: impose a ban 意为实施禁令。

normal.en: The noun and the verb look the same.
normal.cn: 名词和动词拼写相同。

abstract.en: See a wooden sign at a gate.
abstract.cn: 想象大门口立着一块木牌。

abstract.en: See a hand raised to stop a crowd.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手举起拦住人群。

abstract.en: See a red cross over a cigarette.
abstract.cn: 想象香烟上打了一个红叉。

examples.cn: 市里决定禁止在公园吸烟。

examples.cn: 政府解除了旅行禁令。

examples.en: They banned the sale of the old machines.
examples.cn: 他们禁止销售那些旧机器。

dict_mnemonic.text: ban 读来短促有力：一块牌子落下，就是不许。

root: 源自古英语 bannan「召集、宣告」，与中世纪拉丁语 bannum「公告」同源；由公开宣告缩小为官方的禁止，名词即「禁令」。

sensesIntro.en: The act of forbidding and the order itself are one word in two roles.
sensesIntro.cn: 禁止的动作与那份禁令，是同一个词的两种角色。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wooden sign at a gate.

branches.cn: 禁止吸烟

branches.en: ban the sale
branches.cn: 禁止销售

branches.cn: 解除禁令

branches.cn: 实施禁令

branches.en: a travel ban
branches.cn: 旅行禁令

latinIntro.cn: 这个词是英语本族词，与中世纪拉丁语 bannum 有亲缘关系。

definition_zh: 高速公路；（免费）高速干道
definition_en: a wide road with several lanes on which traffic travels at high speed and which usually has no tolls
core_image: 一条没有红绿灯、没有收费站的多车道大路，车流飞快地向前奔涌
scene: 长途巴士驶出城区，车道渐渐变宽，车速也提了起来。 The bus merged onto the freeway and reached the city within an hour.
sceneCN: 这里 freeway 是「高速公路」（第 1 个义项：供高速行驶的多车道干道）；句意是巴士驶上高速后，一小时内就到了城里。

derivatives.zh: 基础词，义为「路；道路」，freeway 由 free 加 way 构成
同以 way 结尾的复合名词，义为「公路；干道」，可含收费站
由 free 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「自由地；不受限制地」

senses.title: A high-speed road without tolls
senses.titleCN: 高速公路；（免费）高速干道
senses.definition: a wide multilane road built for fast long-distance traffic, especially one with no toll gates
senses.definitionCN: 为快速长途车流修建的宽阔多车道道路，尤指不设收费站的干道
senses.example: Traffic on the freeway slowed to a crawl during the rush hour.
senses.exampleCN: 高峰时段，高速公路上的车流慢得像爬行。
senses.why: The word combines free and way, and the core image is a road you can travel freely at speed.
senses.whyCN: 本词由 free（自由的）与 way（路）合成，核心意象是一条可以畅快高速行驶的路。

senses.title: A symbol of fast urban connection
senses.titleCN: 快速通达的象征；城市动脉
senses.definition: the network of such roads treated as a symbol of speed, congestion, or modern urban life
senses.definitionCN: 由这类道路构成的网络，被视为速度、拥堵或现代都市生活的象征
senses.example: The new freeway cut the trip between the two cities to two hours.
senses.exampleCN: 新建的高速公路把两城之间的车程缩短到两小时。
senses.why: Because the road exists to let traffic move freely, it came to stand for fast connection between places.
senses.whyCN: 由于这种路存在的目的就是让车流畅行，它进而引申为两地之间快速连通的象征。

senses.title: The fast lane itself
senses.definition: the lanes or the flowing traffic on such a road, seen as a place or a stream of vehicles
senses.definitionCN: 这类道路上的车道或奔涌的车流，被当作一处场所或一股车流
senses.example: A broken truck blocked two lanes of the freeway.
senses.exampleCN: 一辆抛锚的卡车堵住了高速公路的两条车道。
senses.why: From naming the whole road, usage narrows to the flowing traffic and its lanes within it.
senses.whyCN: 由整条道路的名称，具体化为路上奔流的车道与车流。

intro.en: Freeway is a transparent American compound built from free and way, coined in the early twentieth century.
intro.cn: freeway 是一个结构透明的美式复合词，由 free 与 way 合成，出现于二十世纪初。

items.en: Old English frēo meant free, and weġ meant way or road; both are native Germanic words.
items.cn: 古英语 frēo 意为「自由的」，weġ 意为「路」；两者都是日耳曼语源的本族词。

items.en: By the Middle English period free and way were common words, and compounds such as pathway and highway had already appeared.
items.cn: 到中古英语时期，free 与 way 已是常用词，pathway、highway 等复合词也已出现。

items.en: The compound freeway is generally dated to the early twentieth century in the United States, when planning words for new motor roads were being coined.
items.cn: 一般认为复合词 freeway 于二十世纪初在美国出现，当时人们正为新的汽车道路创造规划用语。

items.en: The free element emphasized that these roads were to be traveled without paying tolls, distinguishing them from toll roads and parkways.
items.cn: 词中的 free 强调这类道路通行时不缴通行费，以此区别于收费公路（toll road）与景观大道（parkway）。

items.en: Today freeway is the standard American term for such roads; British English uses motorway, and highway in America is a broader term.
items.cn: 如今 freeway 是美国对这类道路的标准称呼；英式英语用 motorway，美式 highway 则是更宽泛的说法。

note.en: Freeway sits in a family of road compounds; watch the differences between American and British usage.
note.cn: freeway 属于一组道路类复合词；注意英美用法的差异。

entries.definition: a main public road, in American use a broader term than freeway
entries.definitionCN: 公路；干道，美式用法中是比 freeway 更宽泛的词

entries.definition: the British English term for a high-speed divided road
entries.definitionCN: 英式英语对高速分隔干道的称呼，与 freeway 对应

entries.definition: the state of being free; only shares the free element with freeway
entries.definitionCN: 自由；与 freeway 同含 free 成分，但构词与语义不同

entries.definition: a wide road for fast traffic, sometimes with tolls
entries.definitionCN: 供快速车流行驶的宽阔道路，有时收费，与 freeway 近义

entries.definition: a toll road, the opposite of the no-toll freeway
entries.definitionCN: 收费公路，恰与免费通行的 freeway 相对

entries.definition: another American name for a long-distance express road
entries.definitionCN: 美国对长途快速干道的另一种称呼，义同高速公路

normalIntro.en: Build the word from its two visible parts: free plus way.
normalIntro.cn: 把这个词拆成两个看得见的部件来记：free 加 way。

normal.en: free + way: a way you use for free, without toll gates.
normal.cn: free + way：一条免费通行的路，没有收费站。

normal.en: Compare highway: high way is a high-grade road; free way is a toll-free road.
normal.cn: 对比 highway：high way 是高级公路；free way 是免费公路。

normal.en: British motorway uses motor, American freeway uses free; pair the two terms.
normal.cn: 英式 motorway 用 motor，美式 freeway 用 free；把两个词配对记。

normal.en: Freeway traffic moves fast because there are no lights or booths to slow it.
normal.cn: 高速车流之所以快，因为没有红绿灯和收费亭减速。

normal.en: Family of ways: pathway, highway, freeway, throughway — all end in way.
normal.cn: way 词族：pathway、highway、freeway、throughway —— 都以 way 结尾。

abstract.en: Picture an open gateless road stretching to the horizon: nothing blocks you.
abstract.cn: 想象一条没有闸口、直伸天际的开阔大路：没有任何东西拦你。

abstract.en: Feel the sense of gliding freely forward, lane after lane.
abstract.cn: 体会一条接一条车道上自由滑行向前的感觉。

abstract.en: Link free with freedom of movement: the road gives your car freedom.
abstract.cn: 把 free 与行动自由相连：这条路给了汽车自由。

examples.en: We took the freeway south to avoid the slow coastal roads.
examples.cn: 我们走高速公路向南，避开了缓慢的沿海公路。

examples.en: An accident near the exit left the freeway jammed for miles.
examples.cn: 出口附近的事故让高速公路堵了好几英里。

examples.en: Her new job meant a long daily drive on the freeway.
examples.cn: 她的新工作意味着每天要开车在高速路上跑很长的路。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「福瑞维」——福（free 免费而）瑞（顺利）地维（维持）高速通行，谐音联想帮助记住 free 与 way 的组合，并非真实词源。

root: freeway 为复合词：free（古英语 frēo，自由的）+ way（古英语 weġ，道路）。free 表示「免费的、不受阻碍的」，强调通行不缴费；作为词根 free 还见于 freedom、freely，way 还见于 highway、pathway。

sensesIntro.en: From the concrete road itself, the senses widen to the network and the traffic it carries.
sensesIntro.cn: 义项从具体的道路本身出发，扩展到道路网络与其承载的车流。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wide gateless road where vehicles move freely at speed
core.cn: 核心意象：一条没有闸口的宽阔大路，车辆畅快飞驰

branches.en: the physical multilane road with no toll gates
branches.cn: 设有多个车道、不收费的具体道路

branches.en: free movement of traffic implies fast links between cities
branches.cn: 车流畅行意味着城市之间快速连通

branches.en: the network stands for modern urban life
branches.cn: 路网被视为现代都市生活的象征

branches.en: the lanes and vehicles form a flowing stream
branches.cn: 车道与车辆汇成奔涌的车流

branches.en: congestion on the artery shapes daily commuting
branches.cn: 干道上的拥堵塑造着日常通勤

intro.en: Freeway is a plain compound; the pattern free/way helps you read other road words.
intro.cn: freeway 是个朴素的复合词；free/way 的构词模式能帮你读懂其他道路类词。

latinIntro.en: The two elements are native Germanic, so there are no Latin cognates to list.
latinIntro.cn: 两个构词成分都是日耳曼本族词，因此没有可列的拉丁同源词。

a coastal highway linking the towns
join the motorway at junction nine
items.exampleCN: 在九号路口驶入高速公路

items.meaning: a narrow path or a course of action
items.example: a stone pathway through the garden
a new expressway around the lake

items.meaning: the paved path beside a street
