items.exampleCN: 骑车人不应在人行道上骑行

items.example: goods moving freely across the border
the freedom to choose your own path

definition_zh: 找出……的位置；位于；安置；设立；定位
definition_en: to find the exact position of something, to place it in a position, or to be situated in a place
core_image: 一张摊开的地图上，一枚图钉被按在某个精确的坐标点上
scene: 维修员戴上耳机，用测漏仪贴着墙面慢慢移动。 The needle jumped near the bathroom wall, and that was enough to locate the broken pipe behind the tiles.
sceneCN: 这里 locate 是「找出确切位置」（第 1 个义项：确定某物的位置）；句意：指针在浴室墙边突然跳动，这样就足以找出瓷砖后面那截破裂的水管。图中可辨识物件：测漏仪、耳机、墙面记号、水管剖面图；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 找出……的位置；使坐落于；安置；设立
位于；定居（多用于 be located）

senses.title: Find the exact position of something
senses.definition: to discover the exact place where someone or something is
senses.definitionCN: 发现某人或某物所在的确切地点
senses.example: Rescuers used heat sensors to locate the trapped climbers.
senses.exampleCN: 救援人员用热传感器找到了受困登山者的位置。
senses.why: Latin locare meant 'to place', and locus meant 'place'. The modern verb starts by finding the place that belongs to a person or object: the pin is put back on the map.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 locare 意为“放置”，locus 意为“地点”。现代动词的起点是找到某人或某物所属的那个地点：把图钉重新按回地图上。

senses.title: Be situated: occupy a place
senses.definition: in the passive be located, to be situated in a particular place
senses.definitionCN: 用于被动式 be located，表示位于某个特定地点
senses.example: The laboratory is located on the third floor.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室位于三楼。
senses.why: Once a thing has been placed, the result of that placing is a position. English prefers the passive be located for this state, because the place, not the placer, is what matters.
senses.whyCN: 某物被放置之后，放置的结果就是一个位置。英语用被动式 be located 表达这种状态，因为重要的是地点，而不是放置者。

senses.title: Place something deliberately
senses.titleCN: 安置：有意把某物放在某处
senses.definition: to put or fix something in a particular position, especially as part of a plan
senses.definitionCN: 把某物放置或固定在特定位置，尤作为计划的一部分
senses.example: Engineers located the sensor where the pipe bends.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师把传感器安置在管道弯曲处。
senses.why: This sense returns to the Latin verb's active core: locare is to place. The object is not merely found but deliberately given a position.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项回到拉丁动词的主动核心：locare 就是放置。对象不是被找到，而是被有意赋予一个位置。

senses.title: Establish a business or branch in a place
senses.titleCN: 设立：把机构或分支落户某地
senses.definition: to establish an office, factory, or organization in a particular place
senses.definitionCN: 在某地设立办事处、工厂或组织
senses.example: The company located its regional office near the port.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司把地区办事处设在港口附近。
senses.why: A business chooses a place and then settles there. The verb shifts from a single object to an institution that occupies a site, a common use in commerce and planning.
senses.whyCN: 企业先选择一个地点，然后在那里落脚。动词的宾语从单个物件变成占据场地的机构，这是商业与规划中的常见用法。

senses.title: Pinpoint a fault or cause
senses.titleCN: 确定故障或问题的所在
senses.definition: to identify the exact source of a problem, fault, or pain
senses.definitionCN: 确定问题、故障或疼痛的确切来源
senses.example: The technician located the fault in a single connector.
senses.exampleCN: 技术员把故障定位到一个连接器上。
senses.why: A fault is invisible until it is assigned to a point. Locating it means narrowing the search until one place on the system carries the explanation.
senses.whyCN: 故障在被指认到某个点之前是不可见的。定位故障，就是把搜索范围收窄，直到系统上的某一处承载了解释。

senses.title: Technical positioning: radar, sonar, GPS
senses.titleCN: 技术定位：雷达、声呐与全球定位
senses.definition: to determine the position of an object or signal using an instrument
senses.definitionCN: 用仪器确定物体或信号的位置
senses.example: The system locates the drone within ten metres.
senses.exampleCN: 该系统能把无人机定位在十米范围内。
senses.why: Instruments extend the search: a signal is sent, an echo returns, and the delay is converted into coordinates. The old 'place' is now a mathematical point in space.
senses.whyCN: 仪器延伸了搜索：发出信号、收到回波，再把延迟换算成坐标。原来的“地点”如今成了空间中的数学点。

senses.title: Find a passage inside a larger whole
senses.definition: to find a particular passage, file, or item within a larger document or system
senses.definitionCN: 在较大的文档或系统中找到特定段落、文件或条目
senses.example: She located the relevant paragraph in the online manual.
senses.exampleCN: 她在在线手册中找到了相关段落。
senses.why: The 'map' can be a book, a database, or a filing system. Locating is not discovering a new thing but putting your finger on the known place where it sits.
senses.whyCN: 这里的“地图”可以是书、数据库或档案系统。定位不是发现新东西，而是把手指按到它已知所在的那个位置。

senses.title: Map a gene to a chromosome
senses.titleCN: 基因定位：把基因标到染色体上
senses.definition: in genetics, to determine the position of a gene or sequence on a chromosome
senses.definitionCN: 在遗传学中，确定基因或序列在染色体上的位置
senses.example: The team located the mutation on the long arm of chromosome 7.
senses.exampleCN: 团队把该突变定位在 7 号染色体的长臂上。
senses.why: A chromosome is a linear map, and a gene has an address on it. This specialist sense applies the same 'find its place' structure to molecular coordinates.
senses.whyCN: 染色体是一张线性的地图，基因在上面有地址。这个专业义项把同样的“找到它的位置”结构用于分子坐标。

senses.title: Usage boundary: pinpoint, not merely encounter
senses.titleCN: 用法边界：强调精确定位，而非偶然遇到
senses.definition: a usage limit: locate stresses an exact position; find is broader, and be located describes a state rather than an action
senses.definitionCN: 用法限制：locate 强调确切位置；find 范围更宽；be located 描述状态而不是动作
senses.example: I found an old letter in the drawer, but I could not locate the address on any map.
senses.exampleCN: 我在抽屉里发现一封旧信，却无法在任何地图上确定那个地址的位置。
senses.why: Finding can be accidental and can concern anything; locating requires a position that can be specified. The passive state also blocks the progressive in ordinary description, so 'is located' replaces 'is locating'.
senses.whyCN: find 可以是偶然的，也可以针对任何东西；locate 则要求一个能被指明的位置。被动状态在通常描述中也不用进行体，因此用 is located 而不是 is locating。

intro.en: Locate comes from Latin locus 'place' through the verb locare 'to place'. The English verb is early modern, while the 'find the position' sense is much later. The deeper origin of locus is uncertain.
intro.cn: locate 经由拉丁动词 locare“放置”来自拉丁名词 locus“地点”。英语动词出现于近代早期，而“找出位置”的义项要晚得多。locus 更深层的来源并不确定。

items.en: Latin locus meant 'a place, spot, position'. It also developed the sense 'passage in a book', because a text is a kind of place one visits. Its deeper PIE origin is source uncertain.
items.cn: 拉丁语 locus 意为“地点、位置”，还发展出“书中的段落”义，因为文本也是一种可以被造访的地方。它更深的原始印欧语来源不确定。

items.en: From locus came locare 'to place, put, set'. The verb also meant 'to let out for hire', which survives in the leasing sense of location in some languages.
items.cn: 由 locus 产生 locare“放置、安放”。这个动词还表示“出租”，这一义项在一些语言中保留在 location 的租赁义里。

items.en: English adopts locate in the 17c. with the sense 'to place or establish in a position'. It is a learned Latin borrowing, not an inherited word.
items.cn: 英语在 17 世纪引入 locate，义为“放置或安置于某位置”。它是学术性的拉丁借词，不是继承词。

items.en: The sense 'to find the exact position of' is recorded in the late 19c., first associated with surveying and marking land in North America.
items.cn: “找出确切位置”这一义项记录于 19 世纪晚期，最初与北美土地测量和标界有关。

items.en: Modern English extends locate to faults, files, signals, and genes. Be located becomes the standard way to state where a building or institution stands.
items.cn: 现代英语把 locate 扩展到故障、文件、信号和基因。be located 成为说明建筑或机构坐落何处的标准说法。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin place root or the loc- shape; the second separates finding, situating, positioning, and detecting.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁语“地点”词根或 loc- 词形；第二组区分“找到”“坐落”“安置”和“探测”。

entries.definition: a place or position, or the act of placing something. It is the noun built directly on locate.
entries.definitionCN: 地点、位置，或放置的行为。它是直接由 locate 构成的名词。

entries.definition: a particular area or neighbourhood. It comes from local plus -ity, both from locus.
entries.definitionCN: 特定地区或街区。它由 local 加 -ity 构成，二者都出自 locus。

entries.definition: a railway engine. It joins locus 'place' with movere 'to move', so it moves from place to place, not from locate.
entries.definitionCN: 铁路机车。它把 locus“地点”与 movere“移动”结合，表示“从一地移到另一地”，并非来自 locate。

entries.definition: to discover something, often by chance or after searching. It is broader than locate and does not require an exact position.
entries.definitionCN: 发现某物，常是偶然或经搜寻而得到。它比 locate 宽泛，不要求确切位置。

entries.definition: to place something in a particular context or position. It is formal and common in the passive, like be situated.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物置于特定语境或位置。它较正式，常像 be situated 一样用于被动。

entries.definition: to put something in a chosen place. It stresses the choice of placement rather than the search for coordinates.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物放在选定的位置。它强调有意的摆放，而不是寻找坐标。

entries.definition: to discover that something is present, often with an instrument. It reports presence, while locate reports position.
entries.definitionCN: 发现某物存在，常用仪器。它报告“存在”，而 locate 报告“位置”。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the Latin place word locus, the everyday phrase be located in, and the modern locator and GPS.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：拉丁语地点词 locus、日常短语 be located in，以及现代的 locator 与 GPS。

normal.en: Locus means 'place'; locate is the verb that gives something a place or finds the place it has.
normal.cn: locus 意为“地点”；locate 就是给某物一个地点，或找到它已有的地点。

normal.en: Be located in is the standard phrase for where a building, office, or city stands.
normal.cn: be located in 是说明建筑、办事处或城市坐落何处的标准短语。

normal.en: To locate a fault is to put a finger on the exact point where a system fails.
normal.cn: locate a fault 就是把手指按到系统失效的那个确切点上。

normal.en: A locator is the device that does the locating: a GPS unit, a radio tag, or a sonar beacon.
normal.cn: locator 是执行定位的装置：全球定位仪、无线电标签或声呐信标。

normal.en: Location and locality both come from locus, one naming a point and the other a neighbourhood.
normal.cn: location 与 locality 都出自 locus，一个命名一个点，另一个命名一片街区。

abstract.en: A pin dropped on a paper map: the whole world is flattened, and one point is chosen.
abstract.cn: 一枚图钉落在纸质地图上：整个世界被压平，其中一个点被选中。

abstract.en: A coordinate grid: the place is not a thing but a pair of numbers where two lines cross.
abstract.cn: 一张坐标网格：地点不是一个物件，而是两条线相交处的一对数字。

abstract.en: A searchlight sweeps a dark field, then locks onto one spot; locating is the moment the beam stops moving.
abstract.cn: 探照灯扫过黑暗的场地，然后锁定一处；定位就是光束停止移动的那一刻。

examples.en: The app can locate your phone within a few metres.
examples.cn: 这个应用能在几米范围内定位你的手机。

examples.en: The new campus is located beside the river.
examples.cn: 新校区坐落在河边。

examples.en: Investigators located the leak beneath the kitchen floor.
examples.cn: 调查人员确定了厨房地板下的漏水点。

dict_mnemonic.text: “楼凯特”——凯特在楼里找到了自己的座位 → locate 找到位置

root: 拉丁语 locare“放置”，来自 locus“地点”；核心是“给某物指定或找到它的位置”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of locate, all from the Latin idea of a place: find the place, occupy a place, give a place, settle an institution, pinpoint a fault, fix a signal, find a passage, map a gene, and finally the boundary between finding and pinpointing.
sensesIntro.cn: locate 的九个义项都出自拉丁语“地点”这一观念：找到地点、占据地点、给予地点、让机构落户、锁定故障、确定信号、查到段落、标出基因，最后是“发现”与“精确定位”的边界。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pin is placed on one exact point of a map.
core.cn: 核心意象：一枚图钉被按在地图的某一个精确点上。

branches.en: FINDING: searching ends when the exact point is identified, whether it is a person or a fault.
branches.cn: 寻找：当确切点被认出时搜索结束，无论对象是人还是故障。

branches.en: POSITION: a thing either occupies a place or is deliberately given one.
branches.cn: 位置：某物要么占据一个地点，要么被有意赋予一个地点。

branches.en: INSTITUTIONS AND TEXTS: a branch settles on a site, and a reader puts a finger on a passage.
branches.cn: 机构与文本：分支在场地落户，读者把手指按到某个段落。

branches.en: MEASUREMENT: instruments and genetic maps turn place into coordinates.
branches.cn: 测量：仪器与遗传图谱把地点变成坐标。

branches.en: BOUNDARY: locate demands an exact position, unlike the broader find.
branches.cn: 边界：locate 要求确切位置，不同于更宽泛的 find。

intro.en: Locate is a Latin verb borrowed whole. English adds -ion, -or, -ed and the prefix re- to build location, locator, located and relocate.
intro.cn: locate 是整体借入的拉丁动词。英语通过 -ion、-or、-ed 以及前缀 re- 构成 location、locator、located 与 relocate。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family is built on locus 'place': local, locality, allocate and locomotion all assign, belong to, or move through a place.
latinIntro.cn: 这一拉丁词族建立在 locus“地点”上：local、locality、allocate、locomotion 都涉及指派地点、属于某地或穿行于地点之间。

items.meaning: a place or position; the act of locating
items.meaningCN: 位置；地点；定位行为（-ion 构成行为或结果名词）
items.example: The location of the new station has not been decided.
items.exampleCN: 新车站的位置尚未确定。

items.meaning: a device or person that finds positions
items.meaningCN: 定位器；定位装置（-or 表示执行该动作的物）
items.example: The rescue team carried a radio locator.
items.exampleCN: 救援队携带了一台无线电定位器。

items.meaningCN: 位于……的；坐落于……的（-ed 构成形容词）
items.example: The office is located above the library.
items.exampleCN: 办公室位于图书馆上方。

items.meaning: to move something to a new place
items.meaningCN: 迁移；重新安置（re- 表示“再次、重新”）
items.example: The factory relocated to a larger site.
items.exampleCN: 工厂迁到了更大的场地。

items.example: Every member of the family rests on this noun.
items.exampleCN: 这一词族的每个成员都建立在这个名词上。

items.example: The stem carries the idea of place into English.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干把“地点”带入英语。

items.example: It forms the verb locate from the place noun.
items.exampleCN: 它由“地点”名词构成动词 locate。

items.example: It forms location, the act or result of placing.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 location，即定位的动作或结果。

items.meaning: to place together; to occur together
items.example: The two terms collocate in academic writing.
items.exampleCN: 这两个词在学术写作中常搭配出现。

latinEntries.meaning: a particular place or position; in genetics, the site of a gene
latinEntries.meaningCN: 地点；位置；基因座（直接来自拉丁语 locus）
地方的；当地的（与特定地区有关）

latinEntries.meaning: to assign something for a particular purpose
latinEntries.meaningCN: 分配；拨给（把资源“放置”到某个用途上）

latinEntries.meaning: movement from one place to another
latinEntries.meaningCN: 移动；运动（从一个地点移动到另一个地点）

definition_zh: 同事；同行
definition_en: a person who works with you, especially in the same office or organization
core_image: 同一间办公室里抬头就能看见的那张熟悉面孔
scene: 早会开始前，几个人在茶水间低声交谈。 She asked a colleague to check the numbers.
sceneCN: 这里 colleague 指「同事」（第 1 个义项：同一单位共事的人）；句意是她请一位同事核对数字。

derivatives.zh: 同僚之间互相支持的氛围

senses.title: Someone you work with
senses.definition: a person who works with you in the same office or organization
senses.definitionCN: 在同一办公室或机构与你共事的人
senses.example: My colleague took the call while I was out.
senses.exampleCN: 我不在时我的同事接了电话。
senses.why: The Latin base meant one chosen together, a partner in a shared duty.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词基意为被一起选中的人，即共同承担职责的伙伴。

senses.title: A fellow member of a profession
senses.definition: a person who belongs to the same profession as you
senses.definitionCN: 与您属于同一职业的人
senses.example: She is a colleague from another university.
senses.exampleCN: 她是一位来自另一所大学的同行。
senses.why: Scholars and doctors use it for equals beyond their own office.
senses.whyCN: 学者与医生用它指本单位之外的同行。

intro.en: Colleague comes from Latin collega, from com- together and legare, to choose or send.
intro.cn: colleague 出自拉丁语 collega，由 com-（一起）与 legare（选择、派遣）组成。

items.en: Legare meant to choose, send or appoint.
items.cn: legare 意为选择、派遣或任命。

items.en: Collega named a partner chosen to share an office.
items.cn: collega 指被选中共同任事的人。

items.en: French collègue carried the word toward English.
items.cn: 法语 collègue 把词带向英语。

items.en: English colleague first meant a fellow official.
items.cn: 英语 colleague 最初指同僚官员。

items.en: The word spread to offices, schools and hospitals.
items.cn: 这个词扩展到办公室、学校与医院。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words sharing the colleg- shape, while the meaning group names people who work or stand beside you.
note.cn: 形近组收的是共享 colleg- 形态的词，近义组列出与你共事或同级的人。

entries.definition: a place where students study after school
entries.definitionCN: 学生毕业后继续求学的机构

entries.definition: friendly and equal among people at work
entries.definitionCN: 同事之间友善平等的

entries.definition: a group of teams or countries joined together
entries.definitionCN: 联合在一起的球队或国家

entries.definition: a person who works in the same place as you
entries.definitionCN: 与你同在一处工作的人

entries.definition: a person connected with your work
entries.definitionCN: 与你的工作有关联的人

entries.definition: a person of the same age, rank or ability
entries.definitionCN: 年龄、级别或能力相当的人

normalIntro.en: These hooks read the word as chosen together, then move from the same office to the same profession.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子把它读成被一起选中，再从同一间办公室走到同一职业。

normal.en: Colleague and college share a beginning but not a meaning.
normal.cn: colleague 与 college 开头相同，意思却不同。

normal.en: Two colleagues are two people picked together for one job.
normal.cn: 两位同事就是为同一份工作被一起选中的两个人。

normal.en: The ending sounds like league, a group joined by a common aim.
normal.cn: 词尾听起来像 league，即因共同目标联合的群体。

normal.en: A colleague works beside you, a friend may not.
normal.cn: 同事在你身边工作，朋友却未必。

normal.en: The adjective collegial describes the friendly side of that relationship.
normal.cn: 形容词 collegial 描述这种关系中友善的一面。

abstract.en: Picture two desks facing each other under one lamp.
abstract.cn: 想象两张桌子在一盏灯下相对而放。

abstract.en: Picture a name tag on a door beside your own.
abstract.cn: 想象你门牌旁边的那块名牌。

abstract.en: Picture a hand passing a cup of tea across the aisle.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手把一杯茶递过走道。

examples.en: I share an office with two colleagues.
examples.cn: 我和两位同事共用一间办公室。

examples.en: A colleague from the lab helped me finish the report.
examples.cn: 实验室的一位同事帮我完成了报告。

examples.en: She greeted her former colleagues at the conference.
examples.cn: 她在会议上问候了以前的同事。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 colleague 记成 college 加 ague：同一所学院里一起做事的人，就是同事。

root: 源自拉丁语 collega，com-（一起）加 legare（选择、派遣），本指一起被任命共事的人。

sensesIntro.en: From the person at the next desk to the person in the same profession elsewhere.
sensesIntro.cn: 从隔壁桌的人，到身在别处却与你同行的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a familiar face rising from the next desk.
core.cn: 核心意象：从隔壁桌抬起头来的那张熟悉面孔。

branches.en: The office sense is the everyday one today.
branches.cn: 办公室义是今天最日常的用法。

branches.en: The professional sense reaches beyond one workplace.
branches.cn: 职业义超出了单个工作场所。

branches.en: Both senses rest on shared work rather than friendship.
branches.cn: 两个义项都建立在共同工作上，而非友谊。

branches.en: A colleague is chosen into the same duty, not born into it.
branches.cn: 同事是被选来共担职责的，而不是天生的关系。

branches.en: Researchers call their equals colleagues across the world.
branches.cn: 研究者把世界各地的同行都称为 colleague。

intro.en: The family grows from the Latin root legare, with collegial and collegiate forming the adjective side.
intro.cn: 这个词族从拉丁词根 legare 生长，collegial 与 collegiate 构成形容词一侧。

latinIntro.en: Collega and legare are the Latin sources, and college keeps the same root in a different sense.
latinIntro.cn: collega 与 legare 是拉丁语来源，college 以另一义保留同一词根。

items.meaning: more than one person you work with
items.example: Her colleagues supported the new plan.
items.exampleCN: 她的同事们支持这项新计划。

items.example: Good colleagueship made the work lighter.
items.exampleCN: 良好的同事情谊让工作轻松了些。

items.example: The department kept a collegial tone.
items.exampleCN: 这个部门保持着同僚式的友好气氛。

items.meaning: the quality of mutual support among colleagues
items.meaningCN: 同僚间互相支持的特性
items.example: Meetings are run with real collegiality.
items.exampleCN: 会议在真正的同僚氛围中进行。

items.meaning: a body of people, now a place of study
items.meaningCN: 原指一群共事者，现指学院
items.example: He teaches at a small college.

items.meaning: relating to a college or its members
items.meaningCN: 与学院或其成员有关的
items.example: The team plays in a collegiate league.
items.exampleCN: 这支队伍参加大学联赛。

items.meaning: a group joined for a common purpose
items.meaningCN: 为共同目的联合的群体
items.example: The two towns formed a league.
items.exampleCN: 两个镇结成了一个联盟。

items.meaning: to give a duty to another person
items.example: A good manager knows how to delegate.
items.exampleCN: 好的管理者懂得如何分派任务。

latinEntries.meaning: a partner in office or duty
latinEntries.example: The Roman collega shared power for one year.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 罗马的同僚共同掌权一年。

latinEntries.example: Legare also gives English the word delegate.
latinEntries.exampleCN: legare 也为英语提供了 delegate 一词。

definition_zh: 限制；限制规定；限定
definition_en: a rule or condition that limits what people can do
core_image: 一条画在地上的界线，把可以走的地方收窄
scene: 图书馆对借书数量有严格限制，每人一次只能借五本。 The library has a strict restriction on borrowing: each person may take only five books at a time.
sceneCN: 这里 restriction 是「限制规定」（第 2 个义项：明确规定范围或数量的规则）；句意：图书馆对借书数量有严格限制，每人一次只能借五本。

senses.title: A limit on action
senses.definition: a limit on what someone can do or have
senses.definitionCN: 对某人能做或能拥有之事的限定
senses.example: The restriction on water use lasted all summer.
senses.exampleCN: 用水限制持续了整个夏天。
senses.why: The noun names the result of restricting, so it is the limit itself.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词表示 restricting 的结果，因此就是限制本身。

senses.title: An official rule
senses.definition: an official rule that says what is not allowed
senses.definitionCN: 规定什么不被允许的正式规则
senses.example: New restrictions cover food imports.
senses.exampleCN: 新的限制规定涉及食品进口。
senses.why: A limit written down and enforced becomes a rule.
senses.whyCN: 被写下来并执行的限制，就成了规定。

senses.title: The act of limiting
senses.definition: the act of keeping something within limits
senses.definitionCN: 把某事物保持在界限内的行为
senses.example: The restriction of free speech raises hard questions.
senses.exampleCN: 对言论自由的限定引出了棘手的问题。
senses.why: Restriction can name the process as well as its result.
senses.whyCN: restriction 既能指结果，也能指过程。

intro.en: Restriction adds -ion to restrict, from Latin restrictus, drawn tight.
intro.cn: restriction 在 restrict 上加 -ion，源自拉丁语 restrictus（被拉紧的）。

items.en: Restringere means to draw tight.
items.cn: restringere 意为拉紧。

items.en: Restrictus means drawn tight.
items.cn: restrictus 意为被拉紧的。

items.en: Restrict enters English as a verb.
items.cn: restrict 作为动词进入英语。

items.en: The suffix -ion forms the noun restriction.
items.cn: 后缀 -ion 构成名词 restriction。

items.en: Restrictions now appear in law, travel and trade.
items.cn: restriction 如今出现在法律、旅行与贸易中。

note.en: Restriction is the noun of restrict and is close to limit and rule.
note.cn: restriction 是 restrict 的名词，与限定和规则相近。

entries.definition: to keep within limits
entries.definitionCN: 限制

entries.definition: limiting action
entries.definitionCN: 限制性的

entries.definition: open to few people
entries.definitionCN: 受限制的

entries.definition: a rule that limits something
entries.definitionCN: 限制

entries.definition: an official order against something
entries.definitionCN: 禁令

entries.definition: the power to direct something
entries.definitionCN: 控制

normalIntro.en: Restriction is the noun of restrict: the boundary that has been drawn tight.
normalIntro.cn: restriction 是 restrict 的名词：那条被收紧的边界。

normal.en: Impose restrictions means put limits in place.
normal.cn: impose restrictions 意为施加限制。

normal.en: Lift restrictions means remove the limits.
normal.cn: lift restrictions 意为解除限制。

normal.en: Travel restrictions control where people may go.
normal.cn: travel restrictions 控制人们可以去哪里。

normal.en: Without restriction means with no limit at all.
normal.cn: without restriction 意为完全不受限制。

normal.en: Compare restraint: a restraint is a pull, a restriction is a rule.
normal.cn: 对比 restraint：restraint 是拉住的力量，restriction 是规则。

abstract.en: Picture a line on the floor that nobody may cross.
abstract.cn: 想象地上一条谁也不许越过的线。

abstract.en: Imagine a sign that lists what is not allowed.
abstract.cn: 想象一块列出禁止事项的牌子。

abstract.en: Think of a door narrowed so only one person fits.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇被改窄、只能容一人通过的门。

examples.en: The city put restrictions on new building heights.
examples.cn: 该市对新建筑的高度施加了限制。

examples.en: There are restrictions on taking photos inside.
examples.cn: 馆内拍照有规定限制。

examples.en: The restriction of movement helped stop the spread.
examples.cn: 对人员流动的限定帮助阻止了扩散。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「restrict（限制）＋ ion」——把范围收紧之后留下的那条界线，就是限制规定；这只是构词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 re-（回）＋ stringere（拉紧）→ restrictus（被拉紧的）→ restrict ＋ -ion → restriction，核心义「被收紧的范围或规则」。

sensesIntro.en: Restriction first names a limit, then an official rule, and finally the act of limiting itself.
sensesIntro.cn: restriction 先指限制，再指正式规定，最后指限定这一行为本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line on the ground narrowing the allowed space.
core.cn: 核心意象：地上一条把允许空间收窄的界线。

branches.en: The basic sense is a limit on what may be done.
branches.cn: 基本义是对可以做什么的限定。

branches.en: A written limit becomes an official rule.
branches.cn: 写下来的限定成为正式规定。

branches.en: The word also names the limiting process.
branches.cn: 这个词也指限制的过程。

branches.en: Rules give everyday limits their force.
branches.cn: 规则赋予日常限制以效力。

branches.en: Enforcing a rule is the act of restricting.
branches.cn: 执行规则就是限制的行为。

intro.en: Restriction adds the noun suffix -ion to restrict, whose root means drawn tight.
intro.cn: restriction 在 restrict 后加名词后缀 -ion，其词根意为拉紧。

latinIntro.en: Latin strictus, drawn tight, underlies restrict and restriction.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 strictus（被拉紧的）是 restrict 与 restriction 的根基。

items.exampleCN: restricted 描述受限的进入权限。

definition_zh: 焦虑的；担心的；渴望的；令人不安的
definition_en: feeling worried and nervous about something uncertain, or strongly wanting to do or have something
core_image: 心被一只看不见的手捏着，眼睛不停往未来的方向瞟
scene: 车站广播说列车晚点，母亲一遍遍看表，又望向出口。 The mother was anxious about her son's late train.
sceneCN: 这里 anxious 是「焦虑的、担心的」（第 1 个义项：对不确定之事感到担心）；句意为母亲为儿子那趟晚点的列车而担心。画面里有车站广播、反复看表的母亲与空荡的出口。

pos.zh: 形容词：焦虑的；担心的；渴望的；令人不安的

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ly 构成，义为「焦虑地；急切地」
由本词加 -ness 构成，义为「焦虑；急切」
由 over- 加本词构成，义为「过度焦虑的」
与本词同出拉丁语 anxius 的名词，义为「焦虑；忧虑」

senses.title: Worried about something uncertain
senses.definition: feeling worried and nervous because something is uncertain or may go wrong
senses.definitionCN: 因为事情不确定或可能出错而感到担心和紧张
senses.example: She grew anxious when the test results did not arrive.
senses.exampleCN: 检查结果迟迟不来，她越来越担心。
senses.why: The Latin adjective anxius is literally 'tightened', so the person is pictured with a chest held shut by fear.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁形容词 anxius 字面是「被勒紧的」，所以这个人被画成胸口被恐惧收住的样子。

senses.title: Eager to do something
senses.definition: strongly wanting to do something or to have something happen
senses.definitionCN: 强烈地想做某事或希望某事发生
senses.example: He was anxious to please his new colleagues.
senses.exampleCN: 他急切地想讨新同事喜欢。
senses.why: Wanting pulls the chest just as tightly as fearing, so the same adjective serves both directions of feeling.
senses.whyCN: 「想要」和「害怕」一样会把胸口收紧，所以同一个形容词可以服务两个方向的情绪。

senses.title: Causing worry
senses.definition: describing a period, moment, or situation that makes people feel worried
senses.definitionCN: 形容让人感到担心的时段、时刻或处境
senses.example: There was an anxious silence before the verdict was read.
senses.exampleCN: 宣读裁决之前有一段令人不安的沉默。
senses.why: By a common shift the feeling word comes to describe the thing that produces it, as if the silence itself were tight.
senses.whyCN: 情绪词常发生这样的转移，转而形容引起它的东西，仿佛那段沉默本身就是绷紧的。

intro.en: Anxious is the Latin adjective behind anxiety, imported with the same physical image of a squeezed throat.
intro.cn: anxious 是 anxiety 背后的那个拉丁形容词，带着同样「喉咙被勒紧」的身体意象进入英语。

items.en: The verb angere meant 'to choke, squeeze, strangle' and also 'to torment'; it is shared with anger and anguish.
items.cn: 动词 angere 意为「使窒息、挤压、勒住」，也有「折磨」的意思；它与 anger、anguish 共用这个词根。

items.en: The adjective anxius described a person as 'tightened, uneasy, troubled', not merely as sad or afraid.
items.cn: 形容词 anxius 把人描述为「被勒紧的、不安的、苦恼的」，不只是悲伤或害怕。

items.en: English took anxious from Latin; early uses were close to 'troubled' and 'full of concern'.
items.cn: 英语从拉丁语引入 anxious；早期用法接近「苦恼的」「满怀忧虑的」。

items.en: The sense 'eager to do something' develops in ordinary speech, especially in the frame anxious to please.
items.cn: 「急于做某事」的义项在日常口语中发展出来，尤其见于 anxious to please 这一句式。

items.en: Today anxious covers worry, eagerness, and even the anxious silence that makes others worry.
items.cn: 今天 anxious 覆盖担忧、急切，甚至包括让别人担忧的那种「令人不安的沉默」。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the same Latin family; the near-meaning group gathers worry adjectives that differ in strength and in whether desire is involved.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁词族；近义组收表示担忧的形容词，强度以及是否含「渴望」各有不同。

entries.definition: The noun for the state of worry or eager desire.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「焦虑；渴望」，是本词对应的名词。

entries.definition: The adverb meaning in a worried or eager way.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「焦虑地；急切地」。

entries.definition: The noun for the quality of being anxious.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「焦虑、急切的状态」。

entries.definition: Feeling troubled about a specific problem or possible trouble.
entries.definitionCN: 为具体问题或可能的麻烦而心烦，事由通常说得清，比 anxious 更口语。

entries.definition: Feeling tense and jumpy, especially before an event or performance.
entries.definitionCN: 紧张而容易受惊，尤指在事件或表演之前，偏重身体的紧绷感。

entries.definition: Feeling mildly uncomfortable because something seems wrong.
entries.definitionCN: 因觉得不对劲而略感不适，强度低于 anxious。

entries.definition: Strongly wanting to do or have something, without the worry that anxious carries.
entries.definitionCN: 强烈地想做或想要，但不带 anxious 那层担忧，语气更明亮。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the squeezing root, the anxious to do frame, and the three directions the adjective can point.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用「收紧」词根、anxious to do 句式，以及这个形容词能指向的三个方向。

normal.en: The root angere squeezes the throat, so anxious is a tightened chest.
normal.cn: 词根 angere 会勒紧喉咙，所以 anxious 就是收着的胸口。

normal.en: Anxious about points at a worry; anxious to points at a wish.
normal.cn: anxious about 指向担忧，anxious to 指向愿望。

normal.en: Anxiety is the noun of the same state, with the abstract suffix -iety.
normal.cn: anxiety 是同一状态的名词，带抽象后缀 -iety。

normal.en: An anxious silence is a silence that makes other people anxious.
normal.cn: an anxious silence 是让别人也变得不安的沉默。

normal.en: The family keeps the same stem across anxious, anxiety, anxiously and anxiousness.
normal.cn: anxious、anxiety、anxiously、anxiousness 共用同一个词干。

abstract.en: Picture a bird on a wire, wings half open, never quite settling.
abstract.cn: 想象电线上的一只鸟，翅膀半张，始终落不踏实。

abstract.en: Picture a hand gripping a railing before the stairs are even visible.
abstract.cn: 想象楼梯还没看见，手已经先抓住了扶手。

abstract.en: Picture an envelope held over a candle, not yet opened but already warm.
abstract.cn: 想象一封信举在烛火上，还没打开却已经发烫。

examples.en: The children were anxious about the first day at their new school.
examples.cn: 孩子们为转学第一天感到担心。

examples.en: She was anxious to finish the report before the office closed.
examples.cn: 她急着在办公室关门前把报告写完。

examples.en: An anxious hour passed before the doctor came out.
examples.cn: 令人不安的一小时过去了，医生才走出来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「昂克舍斯」——昂着头、克着心、舍不得放下：焦虑的

root: 拉丁语 angere（勒紧喉咙）→ anxius（被勒紧的、不安的）→ 英语 anxious。同根词有 anger、anguish、angst，名词形式为 anxiety。词义从身体的「收紧」扩展为心理的「担忧」与「渴望」。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses spread from one tightened chest: worry about what may happen, eagerness for what is wanted, and the atmosphere that makes others feel the same.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项从同一个收紧的胸口散开：对可能之事的担忧、对想要之物的急切，以及让别人也产生同感的氛围。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a chest held shut by an unseen hand while the eyes keep looking ahead.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手暗暗收着胸口，眼睛却一直往前方看。

branches.en: THE WORRY LINE: the tightened chest pointed at something uncertain.
branches.cn: 担忧线：收紧的胸口对着某件不确定的事。

branches.en: THE WISH LINE: the same tightness produced by wanting rather than dreading.
branches.cn: 愿望线：同样的收紧由「想要」而非「害怕」造成。

branches.en: THE ATMOSPHERE LINE: the feeling spreads into the room and makes others tense.
branches.cn: 氛围线：这种情绪扩散到房间里，让别人也绷起来。

branches.en: THE MIRROR LINE: the person feels the tightness, and the moment is described by the same word.
branches.cn: 镜像线：人感到收紧，而那个时刻也用同一个词来描述。

branches.en: THE OUTWARD LINE: eager reaching and uneasy air both pull other people forward.
branches.cn: 向外线：急切的伸取与不安的气氛，都会把旁人往前拉。

intro.en: Anxious adds the adjective suffix -ious to the Latin stem anx-, and the family then takes -ly, -ness and the prefix over-.
intro.cn: anxious 在拉丁词干 anx- 上加形容词后缀 -ious；这一族随后再接 -ly、-ness 与介词性前缀 over-。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is anxius, built on angere; anxiety is its abstract noun.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁基础是建立在 angere 之上的 anxius；anxiety 是它的抽象名词。

items.example: It lies under both anxious and anger.
items.exampleCN: 它同时藏在 anxious 与 anger 底下。

items.example: It carries the meaning into English.
items.exampleCN: 它把这层意思带进英语。

items.meaning: the base of the adjectival family
items.example: It appears in anxiously and overanxious.
items.exampleCN: 它出现在 anxiously 与 overanxious 中。

items.example: It forms the sister noun anxiety.

latinEntries.example: It is the direct source of anxious.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 它是 anxious 的直接来源。
它是 anxiety 背后的拉丁名词。
